bookInfo.author: Sima Guang

sentences.zh: 資治通鑑 第258卷

translations.literal: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 258
translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 258

sentences.zh: 【唐紀七十四】 起屠維作噩，盡重光大淵獻，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Tang Records 74] Beginning from tuyuan zuoe, ending at chongguang dayuanxian, altogether three years.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Records 74] From the year tuyuan zuoe through chongguang dayuanxian, covering three years in all.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝上之上龍紀元年（

translations.literal: Above, the first year of Longji under Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, Glorious, Cultured, and Filial (
translations.idiomatic: Above: the first year of the Longji era under Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, Glorious, Cultured, and Filial (

sentences.zh: 己酉，公元八八九年）

translations.literal: jiyou, corresponding to the year 889 CE)
translations.idiomatic: jiyou, A.D. 889)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，癸巳朔，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on guisi the first day of the month, amnesty for all under Heaven, era name changed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (guisi), an empire-wide amnesty was proclaimed and the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎劉崇望同平章事。

translations.literal: Liu Chongwang, Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy and Vice Minister of War, was made Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Chongwang, chief Hanlin academician and vice minister of war, was appointed co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 汴將龐師古拔宿遷，軍於呂梁。

translations.literal: The Bian general Pang Shigu captured Suqian and encamped at Lüliang.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shigu, a general of Bian, took Suqian and encamped at Lüliang.

sentences.zh: 時溥逆戰，大敗，還保彭城。

translations.literal: Shi Pu met him in battle, suffered a great defeat, and withdrew to hold Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu gave battle but was routed and fell back to defend Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 壬子，蔡將郭璠殺申叢，送秦宗權於汴，告朱全忠云：「叢謀復立宗權。」

translations.literal: On renzi, the Cai general Guo Fan killed Shen Cong, sent Qin Zongquan to Bian, and told Zhu Quanzhong, saying, "Cong plotted to restore Zongquan to power."
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Guo Fan, a general of Cai, killed Shen Cong, sent Qin Zongquan to Bian, and reported to Zhu Quanzhong: "Cong was plotting to restore Zongquan."

sentences.zh: 全忠以璠為淮西留後。

translations.literal: Quanzhong made Fan military governor of Huai West.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong appointed Fan acting military governor of Huai West.

sentences.zh: 戊申，王建大破山行章於新繁，殺獲近萬人，行章僅以身免。

translations.literal: On wushen, Wang Jian inflicted a great defeat on Shan Xingzhang at Xinfan, killing and capturing nearly ten thousand men; Xingzhang barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Wang Jian routed Shan Xingzhang at Xinfan, killing or capturing nearly ten thousand men; Xingzhang himself barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 楊晟懼，徙屯三交，行章屯濛陽，與建相持。

translations.literal: Yang Sheng, in fear, moved his camp to Sanjiao; Xingzhang encamped at Mengyang, and the two sides faced each other in stalemate with Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the outcome, Yang Sheng shifted his camp to Sanjiao; Xingzhang held Mengyang, and the two sides settled into a standoff with Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 二月，朱全忠送秦宗權至京師，斬於獨柳。

translations.literal: In the second month, Zhu Quanzhong sent Qin Zongquan to the capital, where he was executed at Duli.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Zhu Quanzhong sent Qin Zongquan to the capital, where he was beheaded at Duli.

sentences.zh: 京兆尹孫揆監刑，宗權於檻車中引首謂揆曰：「尚書察宗權豈反者邪？

translations.literal: Sun Kui, metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, supervised the execution; Zongquan, in the prisoner cart, raised his head and said to Kui, "Sir, do you see that Zongquan is a rebel?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Kui, metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, oversaw the execution; from the prisoner cart Zongquan lifted his head and said to Kui, "Sir, can you truly see Zongquan as a rebel?

sentences.zh: 但輸忠不效耳。」

translations.literal: I only offered loyalty without success."
translations.idiomatic: I merely offered my loyalty, and it came to nothing."

sentences.zh: 觀者皆笑。

translations.literal: The onlookers all laughed.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd laughed.

sentences.zh: 揆，逖之族孫也。

translations.literal: Kui was a descendant of Sun Ti in the same clan.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was a collateral descendant of Sun Ti.

sentences.zh: 三月，加朱全忠兼中書令，進爵東平郡王。

translations.literal: In the third month, Zhu Quanzhong was additionally made Concurrent Director of the Secretariat and advanced in rank to Prince of Dongping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, Zhu Quanzhong was additionally appointed concurrent director of the Secretariat and promoted to prince of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 全忠既克蔡州，軍勢益盛。

translations.literal: After Quanzhong had taken Cai Prefecture, his military strength grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: Once Quanzhong had captured Cai Prefecture, his armies grew stronger still.

sentences.zh: 加奉國節度使趙德諲中書令，加蔡州節度使趙犨同平章事，充忠武節度使，以陳州為治所。

translations.literal: Zhao Dexin, military governor of Fengguo, was made Director of the Secretariat; Zhao Chou, military governor of Cai Prefecture, was made Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and appointed military governor of Zhongwu, with Chen Prefecture as his seat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Dexin, military governor of Fengguo, was made director of the Secretariat; Zhao Chou, military governor of Cai, was made co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery and appointed military governor of Zhongwu, with his headquarters at Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會犨有疾，悉以軍府事授其弟昶，表乞骸骨，詔以昶代為忠武節度使。

translations.literal: When Chou fell ill, he entrusted all military and prefectural affairs to his younger brother Chang, memorialized to request retirement, and an edict appointed Chang to replace him as military governor of Zhongwu.
translations.idiomatic: When Chou fell ill, he turned all military and administrative affairs over to his younger brother Chang and memorialized asking to retire; the court ordered Chang to succeed him as military governor of Zhongwu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，犨薨。

translations.literal: Before long, Chou died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Chou died.

sentences.zh: 丙申，錢銶拔蘇州，徐約亡入海而死。

translations.literal: On bingshen, Qian Liu captured Suzhou; Xu Yue fled to sea and died there.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, Qian Liu took Suzhou; Xu Yue fled to sea and perished there.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐以海昌都將沈粲權知蘇州。

translations.literal: Qian Liu appointed Shen Can, commander of Haichang, to act as administrator of Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu placed Shen Can, commander of Haichang, in temporary charge of Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，賜陝虢軍號保義。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: the Shaan-Guo army was granted the designation Baoyi.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, the Shaan-Guo army was given the designation Baoyi (Preserving Righteousness).

sentences.zh: 五月，甲辰，潤州制置使阮結卒，錢鏐以靜江都將成及代之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on jiachen, Ruan Jie, commissioner of Run Prefecture, died; Qian Liu replaced him with Cheng Ji, commander of Jingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on jiachen, Ruan Jie, commissioner of Run Prefecture, died; Qian Liu appointed Cheng Ji, commander of Jingjiang, in his place.

sentences.zh: 李克用大發兵，遣李罕之、李存孝攻孟方立，六月，拔磁、洺二州。

translations.literal: Li Keyong raised a large force and sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao to attack Meng Fangli; in the sixth month they captured Ci and Ming prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong mobilized a large army and sent Li Hanzhi and Li Cunxiao against Meng Fangli; in the sixth month they took Ci and Ming prefectures.

sentences.zh: 方立遣大將馬溉、袁奉韜將兵數萬拒之，戰於琉璃陂，方立兵大敗，二將皆為所擒，克用乘勝進攻邢州。

translations.literal: Fangli sent his great generals Ma Gai and Yuan Fengtao with tens of thousands of troops to resist; they fought at Liuli Po, Fangli's army was greatly defeated, and both generals were captured; Keyong pressed the advantage and attacked Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Fangli sent his chief generals Ma Gai and Yuan Fengtao with tens of thousands of men to resist; at Liuli Po his army was routed and both generals were taken; Keyong pressed on and attacked Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 方立性猜忌，諸將多怨，至是皆不為方立用，方立慚懼，飲藥死。

translations.literal: Fangli was by nature suspicious and jealous, and many of his generals bore resentment; by this time none would serve him, and Fangli, ashamed and afraid, took poison and died.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious by nature, Fangli had alienated many of his generals; now none would fight for him, and he died by poison, overcome with shame and fear.

sentences.zh: 弟攝洺州刺史遷，素得士心，眾奉之為留後，求援於朱全忠。

translations.literal: His younger brother Qian, who held Ming Prefecture as acting prefect, had long won the hearts of the troops; the men acclaimed him acting military governor and sought aid from Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qian, acting prefect of Ming, had long enjoyed the soldiers' loyalty; they acclaimed him acting military governor and appealed to Zhu Quanzhong for help.

sentences.zh: 全忠假道於魏博，羅弘信不許。

translations.literal: Quanzhong asked passage through Weibo; Luo Hongxin refused.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong asked Luo Hongxin of Weibo for passage through his territory, but was refused.

sentences.zh: 全忠乃遣大將王虔裕將精兵數百，間道入邢州共守。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then sent his great general Wang Qianyu with several hundred elite troops by a hidden route into Xing Prefecture to defend it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then sent his general Wang Qianyu with several hundred picked troops by a back route into Xing to help hold the city.

sentences.zh: 楊行密圍宣州，城中食盡，人相啖，指揮使周進思據城困逐趙鍠。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi besieged Xuan Prefecture; food in the city was exhausted and men ate one another; the commander Zhou Jinsi held the city and pressed Zhao Huang.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi besieged Xuan Prefecture until food ran out and people resorted to cannibalism; the commander Zhou Jinsi held the city and harried Zhao Huang.

sentences.zh: 鍠將奔廣陵。

translations.literal: Huang was about to flee to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Huang prepared to flee to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 田頵追擒之。

translations.literal: Tian Jun pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun overtook and captured him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，城中執進思以降。

translations.literal: Before long, those in the city seized Jinsi and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the townspeople seized Jinsi and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 行密入宣州，諸將爭取金帛，徐溫獨據米囷，為粥以食餓者。

translations.literal: Xingmi entered Xuan Prefecture; the generals vied for gold and silk, but Xu Wen alone seized the granary and made gruel to feed the starving.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi entered Xuan Prefecture; while his generals scrambled for gold and silk, Xu Wen alone took the grain store and made porridge for the starving.

sentences.zh: 溫，朐山人也。

translations.literal: Wen was a native of Qushan.
translations.idiomatic: Wen was a native of Qushan.

sentences.zh: 鍠將宿松周本，勇冠軍中，行密獲而釋之，以為裨將。

translations.literal: Huang's general Zhou Ben of Susong, whose courage surpassed all in the army, was captured and released by Xingmi and made a staff general.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ben of Susong, one of Huang's generals and the bravest man in the army, was captured, released, and made a staff general.

sentences.zh: 鍠既敗，左右皆散，惟李德誠從鍠不去，行密以宗女妻之。

translations.literal: After Huang's defeat his attendants all scattered; only Li Decheng would not leave Huang's side; Xingmi gave him a daughter of his clan in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang was defeated his followers scattered, but Li Decheng alone stayed with him; Xingmi rewarded him with a daughter of his clan in marriage.

sentences.zh: 德誠，西華人也。

translations.literal: Decheng was a native of Xihua.
translations.idiomatic: Decheng was a native of Xihua.

sentences.zh: 行密表言於朝，詔以行密為宣歙觀察使。

translations.literal: Xingmi memorialized the court, and an edict appointed him military commissioner of Xuan-She.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi memorialized the court, which appointed him military commissioner of Xuan-She.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠與趙鍠有舊，遣使求之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong had old ties with Zhao Huang and sent envoys to request him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong, who had known Zhao Huang of old, sent envoys asking for him.

sentences.zh: 行密謀於袁襲，襲曰：「不若斬首以遺之。」

translations.literal: Xingmi consulted Yuan Xi; Xi said, "Better to cut off his head and send it as a gift."
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi consulted Yuan Xi, who said, "You had better send his head as a gift."

sentences.zh: 行密從之。

translations.literal: Xingmi followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，襲卒，行密哭之曰：「天不欲成吾大功邪，何為折吾股肱也！

translations.literal: Before long, Xi died; Xingmi wept for him, saying, "Does Heaven not wish my great enterprise to succeed, that it breaks my arms and legs!
translations.idiomatic: Before long Xi died; Xingmi mourned him, saying, "Does Heaven not want my great work to succeed, that it breaks my right hand and left!

sentences.zh: 吾好寬，而襲每勸我以殺，此其所以不壽與！」

translations.literal: I love leniency, yet Xi always urged me to kill—is this not why he did not live long!"
translations.idiomatic: I love mercy, yet Xi always urged me to kill—is that not why he did not live long!"

sentences.zh: 孫儒遣兵攻廬州，蔡儔以州降之。

translations.literal: Sun Ru sent troops to attack Lu Prefecture; Cai Chou surrendered the prefecture to him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru sent troops against Lu Prefecture, and Cai Chou surrendered the city to him.

sentences.zh: 朱珍拔蕭縣，據之，與時浦相拒，朱全忠欲自往臨之。

translations.literal: Zhu Zhen captured Xiao County and held it, facing Shi Pu in opposition; Zhu Quanzhong wished to go in person to oversee the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Zhen took Xiao County and held it against Shi Pu; Zhu Quanzhong meant to go in person to direct operations.

sentences.zh: 珍命諸軍皆葺馬廄，李唐賓部將嚴郊獨惰慢，軍吏責之，唐賓怒，見珍訴之。

translations.literal: Zhen ordered all armies to repair their stables; Yan Jiao, a subordinate of Li Tangbin, alone was lazy and disrespectful; the army clerk rebuked him; Tangbin grew angry and went to Zhen to complain.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen ordered every unit to repair its stables; Yan Jiao, a subordinate of Li Tangbin, alone shirked the work; when the clerk rebuked him, Tangbin took offense and complained to Zhen.

sentences.zh: 珍亦怒，以唐賓為無禮，拔劍斬之，遣騎白全忠，雲唐賓謀叛。

translations.literal: Zhen also grew angry, deeming Tangbin disrespectful; he drew his sword and killed him, then sent a rider to inform Quanzhong that Tangbin had plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen flew into a rage at what he took for insolence, drew his sword, and killed Tangbin, then sent a rider to Quanzhong reporting that Tangbin had plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 淮南左司馬敬翔，恐全忠乘怒，倉猝處置違宜，故留使者，逮夜，然後從容白之，全忠果大驚。

translations.literal: Jing Xiang, left vice marshal of Huainan, fearing that Quanzhong in anger might act rashly and improperly, detained the messenger until night and only then calmly reported the matter; Quanzhong was indeed greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Xiang, left vice marshal of Huainan, fearing that Quanzhong in his anger might act rashly, held the messenger until nightfall and only then reported the matter calmly; Quanzhong was indeed deeply shaken.

sentences.zh: 翔因為畫策，詐收唐賓妻子繫獄，遣騎往慰撫，全忠從之，軍中始安。

translations.literal: Xiang thereupon devised a plan: falsely seize Tangbin's wife and children and imprison them, and send riders to offer consolation; Quanzhong followed this, and the army at last settled.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang then proposed a stratagem: pretend to imprison Tangbin's family and send riders to console the troops; Quanzhong agreed, and the army calmed.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，全忠如蕭縣，未至，珍出迎，命武士執之，責以專殺而誅之。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: Quanzhong went to Xiao County; before he arrived, Zhen came out to meet him; Quanzhong ordered warriors to seize him, charged him with unauthorized killing, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Quanzhong set out for Xiao County; before he arrived, Zhen came out to meet him; Quanzhong had his guards seize him, condemned him for killing on his own authority, and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 諸將霍存等數十人叩頭為之請，全忠怒，以床擲之，乃退。

translations.literal: Several dozen generals including Huo Cun kowtowed to plead for him; Quanzhong in anger threw a couch at them, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen generals, including Huo Cun, kowtowed to plead for Zhen; Quanzhong in his rage hurled a couch at them, and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 丁未，至蕭縣，以龐師古代珍為都指揮使。

translations.literal: On dingwei he reached Xiao County and appointed Pang Shigu to replace Zhen as overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei he reached Xiao County and appointed Pang Shigu commander in Zhen's place.

sentences.zh: 八月，丙子，全忠進攻時溥壁，會大雨，引兵還。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on bingzi, Quanzhong advanced to attack Shi Pu's ramparts; heavy rain came, and he withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on bingzi, Quanzhong attacked Shi Pu's fortifications, but a downpour forced him to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，平盧節度使王敬武薨。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month: Wang Jingwu, military governor of Pinglu, died.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, Wang Jingwu, military governor of Pinglu, died.

sentences.zh: 子師範，年十六，軍中推為留後，棣州刺史張蟾不從。

translations.literal: His son Shifan, aged sixteen, was acclaimed by the army as acting military governor; Zhang Chan, prefect of Di Prefecture, would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shifan, only sixteen, was acclaimed acting military governor by the troops; Zhang Chan, prefect of Di, refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 詔以太子少師崔安潛兼侍中，充平盧節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Cui Anqian, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, concurrently Palace Attendant and military governor of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Cui Anqian, junior tutor to the heir apparent, concurrently palace attendant and military governor of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 蟾迎安潛至州，與之共討師範。

translations.literal: Chan welcomed Anqian to the prefecture and joined him in campaigning against Shifan.
translations.idiomatic: Chan welcomed Anqian to his prefecture and joined him in campaigning against Shifan.

sentences.zh: 以給事中杜孺休為蘇州刺史，錢鏐不悅，以知州事沈粲為制置指揮使。

translations.literal: Du Ruxiu, Attendant Censor, was made prefect of Suzhou; Qian Liu was displeased and appointed Shen Can, who had been administering the prefecture, commissioner-commander.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ruxiu, an attendant censor, was appointed prefect of Suzhou; Qian Liu, displeased, made Shen Can, who had been running the prefecture, commissioner-commander instead.

sentences.zh: 楊行密遣馬步都虞候田頵等攻常州。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent Tian Jun and others, commandants of horse and foot, to attack Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent Tian Jun and other commanders of horse and foot against Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 十一月，上改名曄。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, the Emperor changed his name to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the emperor changed his personal name to Ye.

sentences.zh: 上將祀圓丘。

translations.literal: The Emperor was about to sacrifice at the Circular Mound Altar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was preparing to sacrifice at the Circular Mound.

sentences.zh: 故事，中尉、樞密皆衣癸衫侍從。

translations.literal: By precedent, the chief eunuchs and commissioners of military affairs all wore guishan robes when attending in service.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, the chief eunuchs and commissioners of military affairs wore guishan robes when attending the emperor.

sentences.zh: 僖宗之世，已具襴笏。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Xizong they already wore formal court dress with tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xizong they had already been given formal court dress and tablets.

sentences.zh: 至是，又令有司製法服，孔緯及諫官、禮官皆以為不可，上出手札諭之曰：「卿等所論至當。

translations.literal: On this occasion he again ordered the relevant offices to prepare ritual court robes; Kong Wei and the remonstrance and ritual officials all deemed it improper; the Emperor sent a personal note instructing them, saying, "Your arguments are entirely correct.
translations.idiomatic: Now he again ordered the offices to prepare full ritual robes; Kong Wei and the remonstrance and ritual officials all objected; the emperor wrote them personally: "Your arguments are entirely correct.

sentences.zh: 事有從權，勿以小瑕，遂妨大禮。」

translations.literal: Matters sometimes require expedient action; do not let a small flaw obstruct a great ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: Yet affairs sometimes require discretion; do not let a minor flaw obstruct a great rite."

sentences.zh: 於是宦官始服劍佩侍祠。

translations.literal: Thereupon the eunuchs for the first time wore swords and girdle ornaments when attending the sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs then attended the sacrifice wearing swords and girdle ornaments for the first time.

sentences.zh: 己酉，祀圓丘，赦天下。

translations.literal: On jiyou he sacrificed at the Circular Mound and proclaimed an amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou he sacrificed at the Circular Mound and proclaimed an empire-wide amnesty.

sentences.zh: 上在籓邸，素疾宦官，及即位，楊復恭恃援立功，所為多不法，上意不平。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was in his princely residence he had long detested the eunuchs; after his accession Yang Fugong, relying on his service in enthroning him, did many unlawful things, and the Emperor's mind was ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: As prince he had long resented the eunuchs; once enthroned, he found Yang Fugong, who had helped put him on the throne, acting lawlessly, and his displeasure grew.

sentences.zh: 政事多謀於宰相，孔緯、張濬勸上舉大中故事，抑宦者權。

translations.literal: State affairs were largely deliberated with the chancellors; Kong Wei and Zhang Jun urged the Emperor to follow the precedents of the Dazhong era and curb eunuch power.
translations.idiomatic: He relied increasingly on his chancellors; Kong Wei and Zhang Jun urged him to follow the precedents of the Dazhong era and curb the eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 復恭常乘肩輿至太極殿。

translations.literal: Fugong often rode in a shoulder-borne carriage as far as the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong often arrived at the Hall of Supreme Ultimate in a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 他日，上與宰相言及四方反者，孔緯曰：「陛下左右有將反者，況四方乎！」

translations.literal: Another day, as the Emperor spoke with the chancellors of rebels in the four quarters, Kong Wei said, "Your Majesty has men about to rebel at your very side—how much more so in the four quarters!"
translations.idiomatic: On another day, as the emperor discussed rebels in the provinces with his chancellors, Kong Wei said, "Your Majesty has would-be rebels at your side already—what of the four quarters!"

sentences.zh: 上矍然問之，緯指復恭曰：「復恭陛下家奴，乃肩輿造前殿，多養壯士為假子，使典禁兵，或為方鎮，非反而何！」

translations.literal: The Emperor started and asked whom he meant; Wei pointed at Fugong and said, "Fugong is Your Majesty's household slave, yet he comes in a shoulder carriage to the front hall, keeps many strong men as adopted sons, puts them in charge of the palace armies, and appoints some to military governorships—if this is not rebellion, what is it!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor started and asked whom he meant; Wei pointed at Fugong: "Fugong is your household slave, yet he comes to the front hall in a sedan, keeps strong men as adopted sons, puts them in charge of the palace armies, and sends some to govern provinces—if that is not rebellion, what is?"

sentences.zh: 復恭曰：「子壯士，欲以收士心，衛國家，豈反邪！」

translations.literal: Fugong said, "Adopting strong men is to win soldiers' hearts and guard the state—how is that rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: Fugong replied, "I adopt strong men to win the soldiers' loyalty and guard the state—how is that rebellion!"

sentences.zh: 上曰：「卿欲衛國家，何不使姓李而姓楊乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "If you wish to guard the state, why do they bear the surname Yang rather than Li?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "If you mean to guard the state, why do they bear the surname Yang and not Li?"

sentences.zh: 復恭無以對。

translations.literal: Fugong had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong had no answer.

sentences.zh: 復恭假子天威軍使楊守立，本姓胡，名弘立，勇冠六軍，人皆畏之。

translations.literal: Fugong's adopted son Yang Shouli, commander of the Tianwei Army, was originally surnamed Hu and named Hongli; his courage surpassed all in the Six Armies, and all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong's adopted son Yang Shouli, commander of the Tianwei Army, was born Hu Hongli; the bravest man in the Six Armies, he was feared by all.

sentences.zh: 上欲討復恭，恐守立作亂，謂復恭：「朕欲得卿鬍子在左右。」

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to move against Fugong but feared Shouli might raise a disturbance; he told Fugong, "I wish to have your bearded son at my side."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to move against Fugong but feared Shouli might rebel; he told Fugong, "I want your bearded son at my side."

sentences.zh: 復恭見守立於上，上賜姓名李順節，使掌六軍管鑰，不期年，擢至天武都頭，領鎮海節度使，俄加同平章事。

translations.literal: Fugong presented Shouli to the Emperor; the Emperor bestowed on him the name and surname Li Shunjie and put him in charge of the keys to the Six Armies; within less than a year he was promoted to commander of the Tianwu Army, made military governor of Zhenhai, and soon after made Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong presented Shouli to the emperor, who gave him the name Li Shunjie and put him in charge of the keys to the Six Armies; within a year he rose to commander of the Tianwu Army, military governor of Zhenhai, and soon co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 及謝日，台吏申請班見百僚，孔緯判不集。

translations.literal: On the day of his thanksgiving audience, the censorate clerks requested that he take his place in the ranks to meet the hundred officials; Kong Wei ruled that the assembly should not convene.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his audience of thanks, the censorate asked that he take his place among the officials; Kong Wei ruled the assembly should not meet.

sentences.zh: 順節至中書，色不悅。

translations.literal: Shunjie came to the Secretariat-Chancellery with an unhappy countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Shunjie came to the Secretariat with a dark look.

sentences.zh: 他日，語微及之，緯曰：「宰相師長百僚，於意安乎？」

translations.literal: Another day, when the matter was lightly touched upon, Wei said, "The chancellor is teacher and elder to the hundred officials—how could he be at ease with this?"
translations.idiomatic: Another day, when the matter came up in passing, Wei said, "The chancellor is teacher and elder to all officials—how could he be easy in his mind?"

sentences.zh: 順節不敢復言。

translations.literal: Shunjie did not dare speak again.
translations.idiomatic: Shunjie did not dare raise it again.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠求領鹽鐵，孔緯獨執以為不可，謂進奏吏曰：「朱公須此職，非興兵不可！」

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sought to head the Salt and Iron Monopoly; Kong Wei alone held firm that it was impermissible, telling the memorial-presenting clerk, "If Lord Zhu must have this office, nothing short of raising troops will do!"
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sought charge of the Salt and Iron Monopoly; Kong Wei alone stood firm against it, telling the memorial clerk, "If Lord Zhu must have that office, he will have to raise troops!"

sentences.zh: 全忠乃止。

translations.literal: Quanzhong thereupon desisted.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong dropped the request.

sentences.zh: 田頵攻常州，為地道入城。

translations.literal: Tian Jun attacked Chang Prefecture and dug a tunnel into the city.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun attacked Chang Prefecture and tunneled into the city.

sentences.zh: 中宵，旌旗甲兵出於制置使杜稜之寢室，遂虜之，以兵三萬戍常州。

translations.literal: At midnight, banners and armored troops emerged in the sleeping quarters of Commissioner Du Ling; they captured him and garrisoned Chang Prefecture with thirty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight banners and armor burst from the bedroom of Commissioner Du Ling; they seized him and left thirty thousand men to garrison Chang.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣龐師古將兵自穎上趨淮南，擊孫儒。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent Pang Shigu with troops from Yingshang toward Huainan to strike Sun Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Pang Shigu from Yingshang into Huainan against Sun Ru.

sentences.zh: 十二月，甲子，王建敗山行章及西川騎將宋行能於廣都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on jiazi, Wang Jian defeated Shan Xingzhang and the Xichuan cavalry general Song Xingneng at Guangdu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jiazi, Wang Jian defeated Shan Xingzhang and the Sichuan cavalry general Song Xingneng at Guangdu.

sentences.zh: 行能奪還成都，行章退守眉州。

translations.literal: Xingneng fought his way back to Chengdu; Xingzhang withdrew to hold Mei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xingneng fought his way back to Chengdu; Xingzhang fell back to Mei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壬申，行章請降於建。

translations.literal: On renshen, Xingzhang requested surrender to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Xingzhang offered to surrender to Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，孫儒自廣陵引兵度江，壬午，逐田頵，取常州，以劉建鋒守之。

translations.literal: On wuyin, Sun Ru led troops from Guangling across the Yangtze; on renwu he drove off Tian Jun, took Chang Prefecture, and left Liu Jianfeng to guard it.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Sun Ru crossed the Yangtze from Guangling; on renwu he drove off Tian Jun, took Chang, and left Liu Jianfeng to hold it.

sentences.zh: 儒還廣陵，建鋒又逐成及，取潤州。

translations.literal: Ru returned to Guangling; Jianfeng also drove off Cheng Ji and took Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ru returned to Guangling; Jianfeng then drove off Cheng Ji and took Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 前山南東道節度使劉巨容之在襄陽也，有申屠生教之燒藥為黃金。

translations.literal: When Liu Jurong, former military governor of Shannan East Circuit, was at Xiangyang, a man named Shentu Sheng taught him to burn drugs to make gold.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jurong, former military governor of Shannan East, was at Xiangyang, a man named Shentu Sheng taught him to transmute elixirs into gold.

sentences.zh: 田令孜之弟過襄陽，巨容出金示之。

translations.literal: The younger brother of Tian Lingzi passed through Xiangyang, and Jurong showed him the gold.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi's younger brother passed through Xiangyang, and Jurong showed him the gold.

sentences.zh: 及寓居成都，令孜求其方，不與，恨之，是歲，令孜殺巨容，滅其族。

translations.literal: When he later resided at Chengdu, Lingzi sought the formula and Jurong would not give it; Lingzi bore resentment; that year Lingzi killed Jurong and exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: When Jurong later lived at Chengdu, Lingzi demanded the formula and was refused; he nursed a grudge, and that year he killed Jurong and wiped out his clan.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝上之上大順元年（

translations.literal: Above, the first year of Dashun under Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, Glorious, Cultured, and Filial (
translations.idiomatic: Above: the first year of the Dashun era under Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, Glorious, Cultured, and Filial (

sentences.zh: 庚戌，公元八九零年）

translations.literal: gengxu, corresponding to the year 890 CE)
translations.idiomatic: gengxu, A.D. 890)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊子朔，群臣上尊號曰聖文睿德光武弘孝皇帝；

translations.literal: Spring, first month, on wuzi the first day of the month, the assembled ministers presented a honorific title: Emperor Sagely, Cultured, Wise, Virtuous, Glorious, Martial, and Greatly Filial;
translations.idiomatic: In spring, on the first day of the first month (wuzi), the ministers presented the honorific title Sagely, Cultured, Wise, Virtuous, Glorious, Martial, and Greatly Filial Emperor;

sentences.zh: 改元。

translations.literal: the era name was changed.
translations.idiomatic: and the reign era was changed.

sentences.zh: 李克用急攻邢州，孟遷食竭力盡，執王虔裕及汴兵以降。

translations.literal: Li Keyong pressed the attack on Xing Prefecture; Meng Qian's food and strength were exhausted; he seized Wang Qianyu and the Bian troops and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong pressed the siege of Xing; Meng Qian, his supplies and strength exhausted, seized Wang Qianyu and the Bian garrison and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 克用以安金俊為邢洺團練使。

translations.literal: Keyong appointed An Jinjun regimental commissioner of Xing and Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong made An Jinjun regimental commissioner of Xing and Ming.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，王建攻邛州，陳敬瑄遣其大將彭城楊儒將兵三千，助刺史毛湘守之，湘出戰，屢敗。

translations.literal: On renyin, Wang Jian attacked Qiong Prefecture; Chen Jingxuan sent his great general Yang Ru of Pengcheng with three thousand troops to help Prefect Mao Xiang defend it; Xiang went out to battle and was repeatedly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Wang Jian attacked Qiong Prefecture; Chen Jingxuan sent his general Yang Ru of Pengcheng with three thousand men to help Prefect Mao Xiang hold the city; Xiang sallied forth and was beaten again and again.

sentences.zh: 楊儒登城，見建兵盛，歎曰：「唐祚盡矣！

translations.literal: Yang Ru mounted the wall, saw Jian's forces were strong, and sighed, "The mandate of Tang is spent!
translations.idiomatic: Yang Ru climbed the wall, saw how strong Jian's army was, and sighed, "The Tang dynasty is finished!

sentences.zh: 王公治眾，嚴而不殘，殆可以庇民乎！」

translations.literal: My lord governs the masses with severity yet without cruelty—perhaps he can shelter the people!"
translations.idiomatic: This lord rules his men strictly but without cruelty—perhaps he can shelter the people!"

sentences.zh: 遂帥所部出降。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his command out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his troops out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 建養以為子，更其姓名曰王宗儒。

translations.literal: Jian adopted him as a son and changed his name and surname to Wang Zongru.
translations.idiomatic: Jian adopted him as a son and gave him the name Wang Zongru.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，建留永平節度判官張琳為邛南招安使，引兵還成都。

translations.literal: On yisi, Jian left Zhang Lin, adjutant of Yongping Circuit, as pacification commissioner of southern Qiong and withdrew his troops to Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi, Jian left Zhang Lin, adjutant of Yongping Circuit, as pacification commissioner of southern Qiong and marched back to Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 琳，許州人也。

translations.literal: Lin was a native of Xu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was a native of Xu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄分兵布寨於犀浦、郫、導江等縣，發城中民戶一丁，晝則穿重壕，采竹木，運磚石；

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan divided his troops and set camps in Xipu, Pi, Daojiang, and other counties; he drafted one man from each household in the city—by day they dug deep moats, gathered bamboo and timber, and hauled brick and stone;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan spread his troops in camps at Xipu, Pi, Daojiang, and other counties, drafting one man from each city household—by day they dug deep moats, cut bamboo and timber, and hauled brick and stone;

sentences.zh: 夜則登城，擊柝巡警，無休息。

translations.literal: by night they mounted the walls, beat clappers on patrol, and had no rest.
translations.idiomatic: by night they manned the walls, beat watch-clappers on patrol, and knew no rest.

sentences.zh: 韋昭度營於唐橋，王建營於東閶門外。

translations.literal: Wei Zhaodu encamped at Tang Bridge; Wang Jian encamped outside the East Chang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaodu encamped at Tang Bridge; Wang Jian outside the East Chang Gate.

sentences.zh: 建事昭度甚謹。

translations.literal: Jian served Zhaodu with great deference.
translations.idiomatic: Jian treated Zhaodu with scrupulous deference.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，簡州將杜有遷執刺史員虔嵩降於建，建以有遷知州事。

translations.literal: On xinhai, Du Youqian, a general of Jian Prefecture, seized Prefect Yuan Qiansong and surrendered to Jian; Jian put Youqian in charge of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai, Du Youqian, a general of Jian Prefecture, seized Prefect Yuan Qiansong and surrendered to Jian, who put Youqian in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 汴將龐師古等眾號十萬。

translations.literal: The Bian generals Pang Shigu and others numbered their forces at one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shigu and the other Bian generals claimed a force of one hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 度淮，聲言救楊行密，攻下天長；

translations.literal: They crossed the Huai, proclaiming that they came to rescue Yang Xingmi, and captured Tianchang;
translations.idiomatic: They crossed the Huai, claiming to rescue Yang Xingmi, and took Tianchang;

sentences.zh: 壬子，下高郵。

translations.literal: on renzi they took Gaoyou.
translations.idiomatic: on renzi they took Gaoyou.

sentences.zh: 二月，己未，資州將侯元綽執刺史楊戡降於王建，建以元綽知州事。

translations.literal: In the second month, on jiwei, Hou Yuanchuo, a general of Zi Prefecture, seized Prefect Yang Kan and surrendered to Wang Jian; Jian put Yuanchuo in charge of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on jiwei, Hou Yuanchuo of Zi Prefecture seized Prefect Yang Kan and surrendered to Wang Jian, who put Yuanchuo in charge of the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，加朱全忠守中書令。

translations.literal: On yichou, Zhu Quanzhong was additionally made Guardian Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Zhu Quanzhong was additionally appointed guardian director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 龐師古引兵深入淮南，己巳，與孫儒戰於陵亭，師古兵敗而還。

translations.literal: Pang Shigu led troops deep into Huainan; on jisi he fought Sun Ru at Lingting; Shigu's army was defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Shigu pushed deep into Huainan; on jisi he fought Sun Ru at Lingting, was defeated, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 楊行密遣其將馬敬言將兵五千，乘虛襲據潤州。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent his general Ma Jingyan with five thousand troops to strike while the enemy was exposed and seize Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent Ma Jingyan with five thousand men to strike an opening and seize Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李友將兵二萬屯青城，將攻常州。

translations.literal: Li You led twenty thousand troops to encamp at Qingcheng, intending to attack Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li You camped at Qingcheng with twenty thousand men, preparing to attack Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 安仁義、劉威、田頵敗劉鋒於武進，敬言、仁義、威屯潤州。

translations.literal: An Renyi, Liu Wei, and Tian Jun defeated Liu Feng at Wujin; Jingyan, Renyi, and Wei encamped at Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An Renyi, Liu Wei, and Tian Jun defeated Liu Feng at Wujin; Jingyan, Renyi, and Wei then encamped at Run.

sentences.zh: 友，合肥人；

translations.literal: You was a native of Hefei;
translations.idiomatic: You was a native of Hefei;

sentences.zh: 威，慎縣人也。

translations.literal: Wei was a native of Shen County.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was a native of Shen County.

sentences.zh: 李克用將兵攻雲州防禦使赫連鐸，克其東城。

translations.literal: Li Keyong led troops to attack Helian Duo, defender of Yun Prefecture, and captured its eastern city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong attacked Helian Duo, defender of Yun Prefecture, and took the eastern city.

sentences.zh: 鐸求救於盧龍節度使李匡威，匡威將兵三萬赴之。

translations.literal: Duo sought rescue from Li Kuangwei, military governor of Lulong; Kuangwei led thirty thousand troops to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Duo appealed to Li Kuangwei, military governor of Lulong, who marched thirty thousand men to his relief.

sentences.zh: 丙子，邢洺團練使安金俊中流矢死，河東萬勝軍使申信叛降於鐸。

translations.literal: On bingzi, An Jinjun, regimental commissioner of Xing and Ming, died of an arrow wound; Shen Xin, commander of the Wansheng Army of Hedong, rebelled and surrendered to Duo.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, An Jinjun, regimental commissioner of Xing and Ming, died of an arrow wound; Shen Xin, commander of the Wansheng Army of Hedong, defected to Duo.

sentences.zh: 會幽州軍至，克用引還。

translations.literal: When the Youzhou army arrived, Keyong withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When the Youzhou army arrived, Keyong withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時溥求救於河東，李克用遣其將石和將五百騎赴之。

translations.literal: Shi Pu sought rescue from Hedong; Li Keyong sent his general Shi He with five hundred cavalry to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Pu appealed to Hedong; Li Keyong sent Shi He with five hundred horsemen to his relief.

sentences.zh: 李克用巡潞州，以供具不厚，怒昭義節度使李克修，詬而笞之。

translations.literal: Li Keyong inspected Lu Prefecture; finding the provisions insufficient, he grew angry at Li Kexiu, military governor of Zhaoyi, reviled and flogged him.
translations.idiomatic: On an inspection of Lu Prefecture, Li Keyong found the hospitality meager, flew into a rage at Li Kexiu, military governor of Zhaoyi, reviled him, and had him flogged.

sentences.zh: 克修慚憤成疾，三月，薨。

translations.literal: Kexiu, ashamed and resentful, fell ill; in the third month he died.
translations.idiomatic: Humiliated and enraged, Kexiu fell ill and died in the third month.

sentences.zh: 克用表其弟決勝軍使克恭為昭義留後。

translations.literal: Keyong memorialized that his younger brother Li Kechong, commander of the Juesheng Army, be made acting military governor of Zhaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong memorialized appointing his younger brother Li Kechong, commander of the Juesheng Army, acting military governor of Zhaoyi.

sentences.zh: 賜宣歙軍號寧國，以楊行密為節度使。

translations.literal: The Xuan-She army was granted the designation Ningguo, and Yang Xingmi was made its military governor.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuan-She army was given the designation Ningguo, and Yang Xingmi was appointed its military governor.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，宿州將張筠逐刺史張紹光，附於時溥；

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month: Zhang Jun, a general of Su Prefecture, drove out Prefect Zhang Shaoguang and attached himself to Shi Pu;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, Zhang Jun of Su Prefecture expelled Prefect Zhang Shaoguang and went over to Shi Pu;

sentences.zh: 朱全忠帥諸軍討之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong led the armies to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong led his armies against him.

sentences.zh: 溥出兵掠碭山，全忠遣牙內都指揮使朱友裕擊之，殺三千餘人，擒石君和。

translations.literal: Pu sent troops to raid Dangshan; Quanzhong dispatched Zhu Youyu, commander of the inner palace guard, to strike them, killing more than three thousand and capturing Shi Junhe.
translations.idiomatic: Pu sent troops to raid Dangshan; Quanzhong sent Zhu Youyu, commander of the inner guard, who killed more than three thousand and captured Shi Junhe.

sentences.zh: 友裕，全忠之子也。

translations.literal: Youyu was Quanzhong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Youyu was Quanzhong's son.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，陳敬瑄遣蜀州刺史任從海將兵二萬救邛州，戰敗，欲以蜀州降王建。

translations.literal: On yichou, Chen Jingxuan sent Ren Conghai, prefect of Shu Prefecture, with twenty thousand troops to rescue Qiong Prefecture; they were defeated, and Conghai wished to surrender Shu Prefecture to Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Chen Jingxuan sent Ren Conghai, prefect of Shu, with twenty thousand men to relieve Qiong; defeated, Conghai meant to surrender Shu to Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄殺之，以徐公鉥代為蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingxuan killed him and replaced him with Xu Gongyue as prefect of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan had him killed and replaced him with Xu Gongyue as prefect of Shu.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，嘉州刺史朱實舉州降於建。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Zhu Shi, prefect of Jia Prefecture, surrendered the entire prefecture to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Zhu Shi, prefect of Jia, surrendered his entire prefecture to Jian.

sentences.zh: 丙子，僰道土豪文武堅執戎州刺史謝承恩降於建。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Wen Wujian, a local strongman of Baidao, seized Prefect Xie Chengen of Rong Prefecture and surrendered to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Wen Wujian, a local magnate of Baidao, seized Rong Prefect Xie Chengen and surrendered to Jian.

sentences.zh: 赫連鐸、李匡威表請討李克用。

translations.literal: Helian Duo and Li Kuangwei memorialized requesting a campaign against Li Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Duo and Li Kuangwei memorialized asking the court to campaign against Li Keyong.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠亦上言：「克用終為國患，今因其敗，臣請帥汴、滑、孟三軍，與河北三鎮共除之。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong also submitted, saying, "Keyong will ultimately be a peril to the state; now that he is defeated, your servant requests to lead the three armies of Bian, Hua, and Meng, together with the three Hebei circuits, to destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong also wrote: "Keyong will be a lasting menace to the realm; now that he is weakened, I ask to lead the armies of Bian, Hua, and Meng, together with the three Hebei circuits, to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 乞朝廷命大臣為統帥。」

translations.literal: I beg the court to appoint a great minister as supreme commander."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the court appoint a senior minister as supreme commander."

sentences.zh: 初，張濬因楊復恭以進，復恭中廢，更附田令孜而薄復恭。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Jun had advanced through Yang Fugong; when Fugong was removed mid-career, Jun attached himself to Tian Lingzi and slighted Fugong.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Jun had risen through Yang Fugong's patronage; when Fugong fell from power, Jun attached himself to Tian Lingzi and turned against Fugong.

sentences.zh: 及復恭再用事，深恨之。

translations.literal: When Fugong returned to power, he deeply resented this.
translations.idiomatic: When Fugong returned to power, he bore a deep grudge.

sentences.zh: 上知濬與復恭有隙，特親倚之。

translations.literal: The Emperor knew Jun and Fugong were at odds and especially favored and relied on Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Jun and Fugong were at odds, the emperor favored Jun all the more.

sentences.zh: 濬亦以功名為己任，每自比謝安、裴度。

translations.literal: Jun also took fame and achievement as his charge, often comparing himself to Xie An and Pei Du.
translations.idiomatic: Jun too made fame his mission, comparing himself to Xie An and Pei Du.

sentences.zh: 克用之討黃巢屯河中也，濬為都統判官。

translations.literal: When Keyong was campaigning against Huang Chao and encamped at Hezhong, Jun was adjutant to the supreme commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Keyong campaigned against Huang Chao at Hezhong, Jun had been adjutant to the supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 克用薄其為人，聞其作相，私謂詔使曰：「張公好虛談而無實用，傾覆之士也。

translations.literal: Keyong held his character in low esteem; hearing he had become chancellor, he privately told the edict envoy, "Lord Zhang loves empty talk without practical use—a man who overturns states.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong despised his character; when he heard Jun had become chancellor, he told the edict envoy privately, "Lord Zhang loves fine talk without substance—a man who overturns states.

sentences.zh: 主上采其名而用之，他日交亂天下，必是人也。」

translations.literal: Our lord has taken him for his reputation and employed him; the day he throws the realm into chaos, it will surely be this man."
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven has taken him for his reputation; when the realm is thrown into chaos, it will be this man."

sentences.zh: 濬聞而銜。

translations.literal: Jun heard of this and bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Jun heard of it and nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 上從容與濬論古今治亂，濬曰：「陛下英睿如此，而中外制於強臣，此臣日夜所痛心疾首也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor spoke at ease with Jun on order and disorder through the ages; Jun said, "Your Majesty is so brilliant and wise, yet within and without you are controlled by powerful ministers—this is what your servant grieves over day and night."
translations.idiomatic: In an easy conversation on order and disorder through the ages, Jun said, "Your Majesty is so brilliant, yet within and without you are controlled by powerful ministers—that is what grieves me day and night."

sentences.zh: 上問以當今所急，對曰：「莫若強兵以服天下。」

translations.literal: The Emperor asked what was most urgent today; he replied, "Nothing surpasses strengthening the army to bring all under Heaven to submission."
translations.idiomatic: Asked what was most urgent, he replied, "Nothing surpasses strengthening the army to bring the realm to heel."

sentences.zh: 上於是廣募兵於京師，至十萬人。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon widely recruited troops in the capital, reaching one hundred thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then recruited widely in the capital until he had one hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 及全忠等請討克用，上命三省、御史台四品以上議之，以為不可者什六七，杜讓能、劉崇望亦以為不可。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong and others requested a campaign against Keyong, the Emperor ordered officials of the fourth rank and above in the Three Departments and Censorate to deliberate; six or seven tenths deemed it impermissible, and Du Rangneng and Liu Chongwang also deemed it impermissible.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong and others asked to campaign against Keyong, the emperor ordered fourth-rank officials and above in the Three Departments and Censorate to debate it; six or seven in ten opposed it, as did Du Rangneng and Liu Chongwang.

sentences.zh: 濬欲倚外勢以擠楊復恭，乃曰：「先帝再幸山南，沙陀所為也。

translations.literal: Jun wished to rely on outside power to squeeze out Yang Fugong, and said, "The late Emperor twice favored Shannan—this was the work of the Shatuo.
translations.idiomatic: Jun wished to use outside force against Yang Fugong and said, "The late emperor twice fled to Shannan—that was the Shatuo's doing.

sentences.zh: 臣常慮其與河朔相表裡，致朝廷不能制。

translations.literal: Your servant has long feared they coordinate with Hebei inside and out, leaving the court unable to control them.
translations.idiomatic: I have long feared they coordinate with Hebei, leaving the court powerless to control them.

sentences.zh: 今兩河籓鎮共請討之，此千載一時。

translations.literal: Now the military governors of both Hebei circuits jointly request a campaign—this is a once-in-a-thousand-years moment.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Hebei governors jointly ask to campaign against him—this is a once-in-a-thousand-years chance.

sentences.zh: 但乞陛下付臣兵柄，旬月可平。

translations.literal: I only beg Your Majesty to entrust military authority to your servant; within a month or so it can be pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Only grant me command of the armies, and within a month or so he can be crushed.

sentences.zh: 失今不取，後悔無及。」

translations.literal: If we miss this moment and do not seize it, regret will come too late."
translations.idiomatic: Miss this moment and regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 孔緯曰：「濬言是也。」

translations.literal: Kong Wei said, "Jun's words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Wei said, "Jun is right."

sentences.zh: 復恭曰：「先朝播遷，雖籓鎮跋扈，亦由居中之臣措置未得其宜。

translations.literal: Fugong said, "The previous reign was driven into exile; though the military governors were overbearing, it was also because the ministers at court did not handle affairs properly.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong said, "The previous reign was driven into exile; though the governors were overbearing, the ministers at court also mishandled affairs.

sentences.zh: 今宗廟甫安，不宜更造兵端。」

translations.literal: Now the ancestral temples have just been secured; we should not stir up warfare again."
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temples have only just been secured; we should not stir up war again."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「克用有興復大功，今乘其危而攻之，天下其謂我何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Keyong rendered great service in restoring the dynasty; if we attack him now while he is in peril, what will the realm say of us?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Keyong restored the dynasty; if we attack him now while he is weak, what will the realm say of us?"

sentences.zh: 緯曰：「陛下所言，一時之體也；

translations.literal: Wei said, "What Your Majesty says concerns present propriety;
translations.idiomatic: Wei said, "What Your Majesty says is a matter of present propriety;

sentences.zh: 張濬所言，萬世之利也。

translations.literal: what Zhang Jun says concerns benefit for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: what Zhang Jun says is a matter of benefit for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 昨計用兵、饋運、犒賞之費，一二年間未至匱乏，在陛下斷志行之耳。」

translations.literal: Yesterday we reckoned the costs of campaigning, transport, and rewards; within a year or two we will not run short—it rests only on Your Majesty's resolute will to act."
translations.idiomatic: We reckoned the costs of war, transport, and rewards yesterday; within a year or two we will not run short—it rests only on Your Majesty's resolve."

sentences.zh: 上以二相言葉，僶俯從之，曰：「茲事今付卿二人，無貽朕羞！」

translations.literal: The Emperor, the two chancellors' words agreeing, bowed his head and assented, saying, "This matter I now entrust to you two—do not bring shame upon me!"
translations.idiomatic: The two chancellors agreeing, the emperor bowed his head and assented: "I entrust this to you both—do not bring shame upon me!"

sentences.zh: 五月，詔削奪克用官爵、屬籍，以濬為河東行營都招討制置宜慰使，京兆尹孫揆副之，以鎮國節度使韓建為都虞候兼供軍糧料使，以朱全忠為南面招討使，王鎔為東面招討使，李匡威為北面招討使，赫連鐸副之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, an edict stripped Keyong of office, rank, and clan register; Jun was made overall campaign commissioner, pacification commissioner, and comfort commissioner for the Hedong expeditionary army, with Sun Kui, metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, as his deputy; Han Jian, military governor of Zhenguo, was made chief commandant and commissioner of army provisions; Zhu Quanzhong was made southern campaign commissioner; Wang Rong eastern campaign commissioner; Li Kuangwei northern campaign commissioner, with Helian Duo as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, an edict stripped Keyong of office, rank, and clan register; Jun was made overall campaign commissioner for Hedong, with Sun Kui, metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao, as deputy; Han Jian, military governor of Zhenguo, was made chief commandant and supply commissioner; Zhu Quanzhong was southern campaign commissioner; Wang Rong eastern; Li Kuangwei northern, with Helian Duo as deputy.

sentences.zh: 濬奏給事中牛徽為行營判官，徽曰：「國家以喪亂之餘，欲為英武之舉，橫挑強寇，離諸侯心，吾見其顛沛也！」

translations.literal: Jun recommended Niu Hui, Attendant Censor, as expeditionary adjutant; Hui said, "The state, in the aftermath of calamity and disorder, wishes to make a heroic stroke, wantonly provoking a powerful foe and alienating the hearts of the feudal lords—I see turmoil ahead!"
translations.idiomatic: Jun recommended Niu Hui, an attendant censor, as expeditionary adjutant; Hui said, "The state, still reeling from chaos, means to strike a heroic blow, wantonly provoking a powerful foe and alienating the governors—I see disaster ahead!"

sentences.zh: 遂以衰疾固辭。

translations.literal: He thereupon pleaded age and illness and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 徽，僧孺之孫也。

translations.literal: Hui was a grandson of Niu Sengru.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was a grandson of Niu Sengru.

sentences.zh: 李克恭驕恣不曉軍事。

translations.literal: Li Kechong was arrogant and willful and did not understand military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kechong was arrogant and ignorant of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 潞人素樂李克修之簡儉，且死非其罪，潞人憐之，由是將士離心。

translations.literal: The people of Lu had long delighted in Li Kexiu's simplicity and frugality, and since he had died though guilty of no crime, they pitied him; from this the officers and soldiers lost heart.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Lu had long loved Li Kexiu for his simplicity and frugality; since he had died though guilty of no crime, they pitied him, and the army lost heart.

sentences.zh: 初，潞人叛孟氏，牙將安居受等召河東兵以取潞州。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the people of Lu rebelled against the Meng clan, the guard generals An Jushou and others summoned Hedong troops to take Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Lu rebelled against the Meng clan, the guard generals An Jushou and others had summoned Hedong troops to take the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 及孟遷以邢、洺、磁州歸李克用，克用寵任之，以遷為軍城都虞候，群從皆補右職，居受等鹹怨且懼。

translations.literal: When Meng Qian surrendered Xing, Ming, and Ci prefectures to Li Keyong, Keyong favored and trusted him, making Qian chief commandant of the army city, and all his kinsmen were given senior posts; Jushou and the others were all resentful and afraid.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Qian surrendered Xing, Ming, and Ci to Li Keyong, Keyong favored him, made him chief commandant of the army city, and gave all his kinsmen senior posts; Jushou and the others were resentful and afraid.

sentences.zh: 昭義有精兵，號「後院將」。

translations.literal: Zhaoyi had elite troops called the "Rear Courtyard Guard."
translations.idiomatic: Zhaoyi had elite troops known as the Rear Courtyard Guard.

sentences.zh: 克用既得三州，將圖河朔，令李克恭選後院將尤驍勇者五百人送晉陽，潞人惜之。

translations.literal: After Keyong had gained the three prefectures and planned to take Hebei, he ordered Li Kechong to select five hundred of the bravest Rear Courtyard Guards and send them to Jinyang; the people of Lu regretted their loss.
translations.idiomatic: After Keyong took the three prefectures and planned to move on Hebei, he ordered Li Kechong to send five hundred of the bravest Rear Courtyard Guards to Jinyang; the people of Lu mourned their loss.

sentences.zh: 克恭遣牙將李元審及小校馮霸部送晉陽，至銅鞮，霸劫其眾以叛，循山而南，至於沁水，眾已三千人。

translations.literal: Kechong sent the guard general Li Yuanshen and the junior officer Feng Ba to escort them to Jinyang; at Tongdi, Ba seized the troops and rebelled, followed the mountains south to Qinshui, and his following had reached three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Kechong sent Li Yuanshen and Feng Ba to escort them to Jinyang; at Tongdi, Ba seized the column and rebelled, marching south along the mountains to Qinshui with three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 李元審擊之，為霸所傷，歸於潞。

translations.literal: Li Yuanshen attacked him, was wounded by Ba, and returned to Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuanshen attacked him, was wounded, and returned to Lu.

sentences.zh: 庚子，克恭就元審所館視之，安居受帥其黨作亂，攻而焚之，克恭、元審皆死。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Kechong went to Yuanshen's quarters to visit him; An Jushou led his faction in revolt, attacked and burned the place, and Kechong and Yuanshen both died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Kechong went to visit Yuanshen at his quarters; An Jushou led his faction in revolt, attacked and burned the place, and Kechong and Yuanshen both died.

sentences.zh: 眾推居受為留後，附於朱全忠。

translations.literal: The masses acclaimed Jushou acting military governor and attached themselves to Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The troops acclaimed Jushou acting military governor and went over to Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 居受使召馮霸，不至。

translations.literal: Jushou sent to summon Feng Ba, but he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Jushou summoned Feng Ba, but he did not come.

sentences.zh: 居受懼，出走，為野人所殺。

translations.literal: Jushou, in fear, fled and was killed by country people.
translations.idiomatic: Afraid, Jushou fled and was killed by country people.

sentences.zh: 霸引兵入潞，自為留後。

translations.literal: "Ba led troops into Lu and made himself acting military governor."
translations.idiomatic: "Ba marched into Lu and made himself acting military governor."

sentences.zh: 時朝廷方討克用，聞克恭死，朝臣皆賀。

translations.literal: At this time the court was campaigning against Keyong; hearing Kechong had died, the court ministers all congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then campaigning against Keyong; when Kechong's death was reported, the ministers congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 全忠遣河陽留後朱崇節將兵入潞州，權知留後。

translations.literal: Quanzhong sent Zhu Chongjie, acting military governor of Heyang, with troops into Lu Prefecture to act as administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong sent Zhu Chongjie of Heyang with troops into Lu to act as administrator.

sentences.zh: 克用遣康君立、李存孝將兵圍之。

translations.literal: Keyong sent Kang Junli and Li Cunxiao with troops to besiege them.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent Kang Junli and Li Cunxiao to besiege them.

sentences.zh: 壬子，張濬帥諸軍五十二都及邠、寧、鄜、夏雜虜合五萬人發京師，上御安喜樓餞之。

translations.literal: On renzi, Zhang Jun led fifty-two army commands of the various forces plus mixed barbarians of Bin, Ning, Fu, and Xia—altogether fifty thousand men—out of the capital; the Emperor attended at Anxi Tower to give them farewell.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Zhang Jun led fifty-two commands plus mixed forces from Bin, Ning, Fu, and Xia—fifty thousand men in all—out of the capital; the emperor saw them off at Anxi Tower.

sentences.zh: 濬屏左右言於上曰：「俟臣先除外憂，然後為陛下除內患。」

translations.literal: Jun dismissed his attendants and said to the Emperor, "Wait until your servant first removes the external worry, then I will remove the internal affliction for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Jun dismissed his attendants and told the emperor, "Wait until I remove the external threat, then I will remove the internal affliction for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 楊復恭竊聽，聞之。

translations.literal: Yang Fugong eavesdropped and heard it.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong overheard him.

sentences.zh: 兩軍中尉餞濬於長樂板，復恭屬濬酒，濬辭以醉，復恭戲之曰：「相公杖鉞專征，作態邪？」

translations.literal: The two army commissioners saw Jun off at Changle Bank; Fugong urged wine on Jun; Jun declined, saying he was drunk; Fugong jested, "Chancellor, bearing the battle-axe on a sole campaign—are you putting on airs?"
translations.idiomatic: The two army commissioners saw Jun off at Changle Bank; Fugong pressed wine on him; Jun pleaded drunkenness; Fugong jested, "Chancellor, bearing the battle-axe on independent command—are you putting on airs?"

sentences.zh: 濬曰：「俟平賊還，方見作態耳！」

translations.literal: Jun said, "Wait until the rebels are pacified and I return—then you will see me putting on airs!"
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "Wait until I return from pacifying the rebels—then you will see me putting on airs!"

sentences.zh: 復恭益忌之。

translations.literal: Fugong came to resent him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Fugong resented him all the more.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，削奪李罕之官爵。

translations.literal: On guichou, Li Hanzhi's titles and ranks were stripped.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Li Hanzhi was stripped of his titles and ranks.

sentences.zh: 六月，以孫揆為昭義節度使，充招討副使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Sun Kui was made military governor of Zhaoyi and appointed deputy campaign commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, Sun Kui was appointed military governor of Zhaoyi and deputy campaign commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，茂州刺史李繼昌帥眾救成都，己未，王建擊斬之。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Li Jichang, prefect of Mao Prefecture, led troops to rescue Chengdu; on jiwei, Wang Jian attacked and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Li Jichang, prefect of Mao, marched to relieve Chengdu; on jiwei, Wang Jian attacked and killed him.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，資簡都制置應援使謝從本殺雅州刺史張承簡，舉城降建。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Xie Congben, overall commissioner for Zi and Jian and relief envoy, killed Zhang Chengjian, prefect of Ya Prefecture, and surrendered the city to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Xie Congben, commissioner for Zi-Jian and relief envoy, killed Prefect Zhang Chengjian of Ya and surrendered the city to Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 孫儒求好於朱全忠，全忠表為淮南節度使。

translations.literal: Sun Ru sought friendship with Zhu Quanzhong; Quanzhong memorialized to appoint him military governor of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru sought an alliance with Zhu Quanzhong, who memorialized to make him military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，全忠殺其使者，遂復為仇敵。

translations.literal: Before long, Quanzhong killed his envoy, and they became enemies again.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Quanzhong killed Ru's envoy, and they were enemies once more.

sentences.zh: 光啟末，德州刺史盧彥威逐義昌節度使楊全玫，自稱留後，求旌節，朝廷未許。

translations.literal: At the end of the Guangqi era, Lu Yanwei, prefect of De Prefecture, drove off Yang Quanmei, military governor of Yichang, styled himself acting governor, and sought the commission and standard—the court did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Guangqi era, Lu Yanwei, prefect of De, expelled Yang Quanmei, military governor of Yichang, declared himself acting governor, and sought formal appointment, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 至是，王鎔、羅弘信因張濬用兵，為之請，乃以彥威為義昌節度使。

translations.literal: At this time, Wang Rong and Luo Hongxin, because Zhang Jun was deploying troops, petitioned on his behalf, and Yanwei was appointed military governor of Yichang.
translations.idiomatic: Now Wang Rong and Luo Hongxin, in connection with Zhang Jun's campaign, petitioned on Yanwei's behalf, and he was appointed military governor of Yichang.

sentences.zh: 張濬會宣武、鎮國、靜難、鳳翔、保大、定難諸軍於晉州。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun assembled the armies of Xuanwu, Zhenguo, Jingnan, Fengxiang, Baoda, and Dingnan at Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun gathered the Xuanwu, Zhenguo, Jingnan, Fengxiang, Baoda, and Dingnan armies at Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 更命義成軍曰宣義。

translations.literal: The Yicheng Army was renamed Xuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: The Yicheng Army was renamed Xuanyi.

sentences.zh: 辛未，以朱全忠為宣武、宣義節度使。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Zhu Quanzhong was made military governor of both Xuanwu and Xuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Zhu Quanzhong was appointed military governor of Xuanwu and Xuanyi.

sentences.zh: 全忠以方有事徐、楊，徵兵遣戍，殊為遼闊，乃辭宣義，請以胡真為節度使，從之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong, being engaged with Xu and Yang, found conscripting troops and sending them to garrison duty extremely remote, and so declined Xuanyi, requesting that Hu Zhen be made military governor—and the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong, already occupied with Xu and Yang, found raising and posting troops there prohibitively distant; he declined Xuanyi and asked that Hu Zhen be appointed military governor instead, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 然後賦出入，皆制於全忠，一如巡屬。

translations.literal: Thereafter revenue and expenditure were all controlled by Quanzhong, just as if it were a prefecture under his patrol.
translations.idiomatic: Revenue and expenditure there were thereafter controlled entirely by Quanzhong, as if the circuit were simply another prefecture under his command.

sentences.zh: 及胡真入為統軍，竟以全忠為兩鎮節度使，罷淮南不領焉。

translations.literal: When Hu Zhen entered the capital as overall commander, Quanzhong was in the end made military governor of both circuits, and his Huainan post was abolished—he did not hold it.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Zhen was recalled to the capital as overall commander, Quanzhong was ultimately given both circuits and relieved of Huainan, which he no longer held.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，官軍至陰地關，朱全忠遣驍將葛從周將千騎，潛自壺關夜抵潞州，犯圍入城。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month: the imperial armies reached Yindi Pass; Zhu Quanzhong sent his fierce general Ge Congzhou with a thousand horsemen to steal from Huguan Pass by night to reach Lu Prefecture, break through the siege, and enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn the imperial armies reached Yindi Pass; Zhu Quanzhong sent his fierce general Ge Congzhou with a thousand cavalry to slip from Huguan by night to Luzhou, break through the siege, and enter the city.

sentences.zh: 又遣別將李讜、李重胤、鄧季筠將兵攻李罕之於澤州，又遣張全義、朱友裕軍於澤州之北，為從周應援。

translations.literal: He also sent the separate generals Li Kan, Li Chongyin, and Deng Jiyun with troops to attack Li Hanzhi at Ze Prefecture, and also sent Zhang Quanyi and Zhu Youyu to encamp north of Ze Prefecture to support Congzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Li Kan, Li Chongyin, and Deng Jiyun against Li Hanzhi at Zezhou, and posted Zhang Quanyi and Zhu Youyu north of Zezhou to support Congzhou.

sentences.zh: 季筠，下邑人也。

translations.literal: Jiyun was a man of Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiyun was from Xiayi.

sentences.zh: 全忠奏：「臣已遣兵守潞州，請孫揆赴鎮。」

translations.literal: Quanzhong memorialized: "Your servant has already sent troops to hold Lu Prefecture; I request that Sun Kui proceed to take up his command."
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong memorialized: "I have already sent troops to hold Luzhou and ask that Sun Kui proceed to take up his post."

sentences.zh: 張濬亦恐昭義遂為汴人所據，分兵二千，使揆將之趣潞州。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun also feared that Zhaoyi would be seized by the men of Bian; he divided out two thousand troops and had Kui lead them hastily to Lu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, fearing Zhaoyi would fall to the Bianzhou men, detached two thousand troops and had Kui lead them posthaste to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，乙丑，揆發晉州，李存孝聞之，以三百騎伏於長子西谷中。

translations.literal: Eighth month, on yichou, Kui set out from Jin Prefecture; Li Cunxiao, hearing of it, lay in ambush with three hundred horsemen in the western valley of Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on yichou, Kui set out from Jinzhou; Li Cunxiao, hearing of it, ambushed him with three hundred cavalry in the western valley of Changzi.

sentences.zh: 揆建牙杖節，褒衣大蓋，擁眾而行。

translations.literal: Kui raised his command pennant and carried the commission baton, wore ceremonial robes and a great canopy, and proceeded surrounded by his masses.
translations.idiomatic: Kui rode forth with command pennant and torch of office, in ceremonial robes beneath a great canopy, surrounded by his escort.

sentences.zh: 存孝突出，擒揆及賜旌節中使韓歸范、牙兵五百餘人，追擊餘眾於刁黃嶺，盡殺之。

translations.literal: Cunxiao burst forth, captured Kui together with the envoy Han Guifan who had come to confer the standard and commission and more than five hundred guard soldiers, pursued the remainder at Diaohuang Ridge, and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao burst out, captured Kui along with the envoy Han Guifan, who had come to confer the commission, and more than five hundred guards; he pursued the rest to Diaohuang Ridge and slaughtered them.

sentences.zh: 存孝械揆及歸范，絲斥以素練，徇於潞州城下曰：「朝廷以孫尚書為潞帥，命韓天使賜旌節，葛僕射可速歸大梁，令尚書視事。」

translations.literal: Cunxiao shackled Kui and Guifan, bound them with white cord, and paraded them beneath the walls of Lu Prefecture, saying, "The court has appointed Minister Sun as commander of Lu; it has ordered Envoy Han to confer the standard and commission. Vice Director Ge should speed back to Daliang and let the Minister take up his duties."
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao put Kui and Guifan in fetters, shackled them with white cord, and paraded them beneath the walls of Luzhou, proclaiming, "The court has appointed Minister Sun commander of Lu and sent Envoy Han to confer the commission. Vice Director Ge should return at once to Daliang and let the Minister take office."

sentences.zh: 遂絲斥以獻於克用。

translations.literal: Then he shackled them and presented them to Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Then he had them bound and presented to Li Keyong.

sentences.zh: 克用囚之，既而使人誘之，欲以為河東副使。

translations.literal: Keyong imprisoned them; afterward he sent men to entice Kui, wishing to make him deputy military governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong held them prisoner, then sent men to win Kui over, intending to make him deputy military governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 揆曰：「吾天子大臣，兵敗而死，分也，豈能伏事鎮使邪！」

translations.literal: Kui said, "I am a minister of the Son of Heaven; to die after defeat in battle is my portion—how could I submit and serve a military governor!"
translations.idiomatic: Kui said, "I am a minister of the emperor; to die in defeat is my lot—how could I bow and serve a military governor!"

sentences.zh: 克用怒，命以鋸鋸之，鋸不能入。

translations.literal: Keyong was enraged and ordered that he be sawn apart; the saw could not bite in.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was furious and ordered him sawn apart; the saw would not cut.

sentences.zh: 揆罵曰：「死狗奴！

translations.literal: Kui cursed, "Dead dog-slave!
translations.idiomatic: Kui cursed, "You dead dog-slave!

sentences.zh: 鋸人當用板夾，汝豈知邪！」

translations.literal: When sawing a man one should use boards to clamp him—do you not even know that!"
translations.idiomatic: When you saw a man you use boards to hold him—don't you even know that!"

sentences.zh: 乃以板夾之，至死，罵不絕聲。

translations.literal: Then they clamped him with boards; until death he did not cease cursing.
translations.idiomatic: They clamped him between boards; he cursed without ceasing until he died.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，孫儒攻潤州。

translations.literal: On bingyin, Sun Ru attacked Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, Sun Ru attacked Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 蘇州刺史杜孺休到官，錢鏐密使沈粲害之。

translations.literal: When Du Ruxiu reached office as prefect of Su Prefecture, Qian Liu secretly sent Shen Can to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When Du Ruxiu took office as prefect of Su, Qian Liu secretly sent Shen Can to assassinate him.

sentences.zh: 會楊行密將李友拔蘇州，粲歸杭州。

translations.literal: Just then Li You, a general of Yang Xingmi, captured Su Prefecture; Can returned to Hang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Yang Xingmi's general Li You took Suzhou, and Can returned to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 鏐欲歸罪於粲而殺之，粲奔孫儒。

translations.literal: Liu wished to lay the blame on Can and kill him; Can fled to Sun Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Liu meant to pin the crime on Can and kill him; Can fled to Sun Ru.

sentences.zh: 王建退屯漢州。

translations.literal: Wang Jian withdrew and encamped at Han Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian withdrew to Hanzhou.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄括富民財以供軍，置征督院，逼以桎梏棰楚，使各自佔。

translations.literal: Chen Jingxuan extorted the wealth of prosperous households to supply the army; he established a collection and enforcement office, forced them with cangue, stocks, and beatings, and made each declare his holdings.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan squeezed wealth from prosperous households to supply the army, set up a collection and enforcement office, and used fetters and beatings to force each man to declare his assets.

sentences.zh: 凡有財者如匿贓、虛占，急征，鹹不聊生。

translations.literal: Every man of wealth was treated as if concealing booty or making false declarations; levies were urgent, and all could barely live.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone with property was treated as if hiding illicit goods or lying on his declaration; levies were relentless, and none could make a living.

sentences.zh: 李罕之告急於李克用，克用遣李存孝將五千騎救之。

translations.literal: Li Hanzhi appealed to Li Keyong in emergency; Keyong sent Li Cunxiao with five thousand horsemen to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hanzhi sent an urgent appeal to Li Keyong, who dispatched Li Cunxiao with five thousand cavalry to relieve him.

sentences.zh: 九月，壬寅，朱全忠軍於河陽。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on renyin, Zhu Quanzhong encamped at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on renyin, Zhu Quanzhong encamped at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 汴軍之初圍澤州也，呼李罕之曰：「相公每恃河東，輕絕當道。

translations.literal: When the Bian army first besieged Ze Prefecture, they called out to Li Hanzhi, "Lord Chancellor, you always rely on Hedong and lightly cut yourself off from the circuit here.
translations.idiomatic: When the Bian army first besieged Zezhou, they shouted to Li Hanzhi, "Lord Chancellor, you always lean on Hedong and treat this circuit with contempt.

sentences.zh: 今張相公圍太原，葛僕射入潞府，旬日之間，沙陀無穴自藏，相公何路求生邪！」

translations.literal: Now Chancellor Zhang is besieging Taiyuan and Vice Director Ge has entered the Lu prefectural seat; within ten days the Shatuo will have no hole to hide in—by what road will the Lord Chancellor seek to live!"
translations.idiomatic: Now Chancellor Zhang besieges Taiyuan and Vice Director Ge holds the Lu prefectural seat; within ten days the Shatuo will have nowhere to hide—what path of escape do you have left!"

sentences.zh: 及李存孝至，選精騎五百，繞汴寨呼曰：「我，沙陀之求穴者也，欲得爾肉以飽士卒，可令肥者出鬥！」

translations.literal: When Li Cunxiao arrived, he selected five hundred elite horsemen, rode around the Bian encampment calling out, "I am he of the Shatuo who seeks their hole; I want your flesh to fill my soldiers—let the fat ones come out and fight!"
translations.idiomatic: When Li Cunxiao arrived, he picked five hundred elite cavalry, circled the Bian camp, and shouted, "I am the Shatuo come to find your hole; I want your flesh to feed my men—send out your fat ones to fight!"

sentences.zh: 汴將鄧季筠，亦驍將也，引兵出戰，存孝生擒之。

translations.literal: The Bian general Deng Jiyun, also a fierce fighter, led troops out to battle; Cunxiao captured him alive.
translations.idiomatic: The Bian general Deng Jiyun, himself a fierce fighter, sallied forth; Cunxiao took him alive.

sentences.zh: 是夕，李讜、李重胤收眾遁去，存孝、罕之隨而擊之，至馬牢山，大破之，斬獲萬計，追至懷州而還。

translations.literal: That evening Li Kan and Li Chongyin gathered their forces and fled; Cunxiao and Hanzhi pursued and struck them, reaching Malao Mountain, inflicting a great defeat; those killed and captured numbered in the tens of thousands; they pursued to Huai Prefecture and returned.
translations.idiomatic: That night Li Kan and Li Chongyin withdrew with their troops; Cunxiao and Hanzhi pursued, routed them at Malao Mountain, killed and captured by the ten thousand, and chased them to Huaizhou before turning back.

sentences.zh: 存孝復引兵攻潞州，葛從周、朱崇節棄潞州而歸。

translations.literal: Cunxiao again led troops to attack Lu Prefecture; Ge Congzhou and Zhu Chongjie abandoned Lu Prefecture and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao again marched on Luzhou; Ge Congzhou and Zhu Chongjie abandoned the city and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 戊申，全忠庭責諸將橈之罪，斬李讜、李重胤而還。

translations.literal: On wushen, Quanzhong publicly charged the generals with the crime of disobedience in court, beheaded Li Kan and Li Chongyin, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Quanzhong held a court assembly to condemn his generals for dereliction, executed Li Kan and Li Chongyin, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 李克用以康君立為昭義留後，李存孝為汾州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Keyong made Kang Junli acting governor of Zhaoyi and Li Cunxiao prefect of Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong appointed Kang Junli acting governor of Zhaoyi and Li Cunxiao prefect of Fen.

sentences.zh: 存孝自謂擒孫揆功大，當鎮昭義，而君立得之，憤恚不食者數日，縱意刑殺，始有叛克用之志。

translations.literal: Cunxiao considered that his achievement in capturing Sun Kui was great and that he ought to govern Zhaoyi, yet Junli obtained it; enraged, he refused food for several days, indulged himself in punishments and killings, and first conceived the will to rebel against Keyong.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao believed his capture of Sun Kui merited command of Zhaoyi, but Junli got the post; furious, he went without food for days, indulged in arbitrary executions, and first began to plot rebellion against Keyong.

sentences.zh: 李匡威攻蔚州，虜其刺史邢善益，赫連鐸引吐蕃、黠戛斯眾數萬攻遮虜平，殺其軍使劉鬍子。

translations.literal: Li Kuangwei attacked Wei Prefecture and captured its prefect Xing Shanyi; Helian Duo led tens of thousands of Tibetans and Kirghiz to attack Zheluping and killed its army commissioner Liu Huzi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei attacked Weizhou and captured Prefect Xing Shanyi; Helian Duo led tens of thousands of Tibetans and Kirghiz against Zheluping and killed Army Commissioner Liu Huzi.

sentences.zh: 克用遣其將李存信擊之，不勝；

translations.literal: Keyong sent his general Li Cunxin to strike them, but he was not victorious;
translations.idiomatic: Keyong sent his general Li Cunxin against them, but he was beaten;

sentences.zh: 更命李嗣源為存信之副，遂破之。

translations.literal: He then appointed Li Siyuan as Cunxin's deputy, and they thereupon defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Li Siyuan as Cunxin's second in command, and they routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 克用以大軍繼其後，匡威、鐸皆敗走，獲匡威之子武州刺史仁宗及鐸之婿，俘斬萬計。
