translations.literal: Keyong followed with a large army; Kuangwei and Duo both fled in defeat; he captured Kuangwei's son Renzong, prefect of Wu Prefecture, and Duo's son-in-law; prisoners killed and captured numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong followed with the main army; Kuangwei and Duo both fled in defeat; he captured Kuangwei's son Renzong, prefect of Wu, and Duo's son-in-law; the dead and captured numbered in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源性謹重廉儉，諸將相會，各自詫勇略，嗣源獨默然，徐曰：「諸君喜以口擊賊，嗣源但以手擊賊耳。」

translations.literal: Li Siyuan was by nature careful, solemn, and frugal; when the generals met, each vaunted his courage and strategy; Siyuan alone remained silent, then said slowly, "You gentlemen delight in striking the enemy with your mouths; Siyuan strikes the enemy only with his hands."
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan was sober, grave, and frugal by nature; when the generals gathered, each bragged of his courage and skill; Siyuan alone said nothing, then remarked quietly, "You gentlemen prefer to strike the enemy with your tongues; I strike the enemy with my hands."

sentences.zh: 眾慚而止。

translations.literal: The assembly was ashamed and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The others fell silent in shame.

sentences.zh: 楊行密以其將張行周為常州制置使。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi appointed his general Zhang Xingzhou commissioner for Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi made his general Zhang Xingzhou commissioner of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 閏月，孫儒遣劉建鋒攻拔常州，殺行周，遂圍蘇州。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, Sun Ru sent Liu Jianfeng to attack and capture Chang Prefecture, killed Xingzhou, and then besieged Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month, Sun Ru sent Liu Jianfeng to take Changzhou, killed Xingzhou, and then besieged Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 邛州刺史毛湘，本田令孜親吏，王建攻之急，食盡，救兵不至。

translations.literal: Mao Xiang, prefect of Qiong Prefecture, had originally been a close attendant of Tian Lingzi; Jian pressed the attack fiercely; provisions were exhausted and relief did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Xiang, prefect of Qiong, had once been a close attendant of Tian Lingzi; Wang Jian pressed the siege hard; food ran out and no relief came.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，湘謂都知兵馬使任可知曰：「吾不忍負田軍容，吏民何罪！

translations.literal: On renxu, Xiang said to Ren Kezhi, overall commander of the army, "I cannot bear to fail Military Commissioner Tian—what crime have the officials and people committed!
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Xiang told Ren Kezhi, the army commander, "I cannot fail Military Commissioner Tian—what fault is there in the officials and people!

sentences.zh: 爾可持吾頭歸王建。」

translations.literal: You may take my head and surrender to Wang Jian."
translations.idiomatic: Take my head and surrender to Wang Jian."

sentences.zh: 乃沐浴以俟刃。

translations.literal: Then he bathed and waited for the blade.
translations.idiomatic: He bathed and waited for the sword.

sentences.zh: 可知斬湘及二子降於建，士民皆泣。

translations.literal: Kezhi beheaded Xiang and his two sons and surrendered to Jian; soldiers and people all wept.
translations.idiomatic: Kezhi beheaded Xiang and his two sons and surrendered to Wang Jian; soldiers and citizens wept.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，建持永平旌節入邛州，以節度判官張琳知留後。

translations.literal: On jiaxu, Jian entered Qiong Prefecture bearing the Yongping standard and commission and made Zhang Lin, chief aide of the circuit, acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu, Wang Jian entered Qiong bearing the Yongping commission and made circuit aide Zhang Lin acting governor.

sentences.zh: 繕完城隍，撫安夷獠，經營蜀、雅。

translations.literal: He repaired the walls and moats, soothed the Yi and Liao tribes, and set in order Shu and Ya.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the walls and defenses, pacified the tribal peoples, and consolidated control over Shu and Ya.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，癸未朔，建引兵還成都，蜀州將李行周逐徐公鉥，舉城降建。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, first day guawei: Jian led troops back to Chengdu; Li Xingzhou, a general of Shu Prefecture, drove off Xu Gongshu and surrendered the city to Jian.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter, on the first day guawei, Wang Jian marched back to Chengdu; Shu general Li Xingzhou expelled Xu Gongshu and surrendered the city to him.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，朱全忠自河陽如滑州視事，遣使者請糧馬及假道於魏以伐河東，羅弘信不許，又請於鎮，鎮人亦不許。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Zhu Quanzhong went from Heyang to Hua Prefecture to take up affairs, sent envoys requesting grain, horses, and passage through Wei to attack Hedong; Luo Hongxin did not grant it; he asked again at Zhen; the people of Zhen also did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Zhu Quanzhong went from Heyang to Huazhou to take up his duties, sent envoys requesting grain, horses, and passage through Wei to attack Hedong; Luo Hongxin refused; he asked at Zhen as well, and the Zhenzhou men refused too.

sentences.zh: 全忠乃自黎陽濟河擊魏。

translations.literal: Quanzhong then crossed the river from Liyang and attacked Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong then crossed the river from Liyang and attacked Wei.

sentences.zh: 加邠寧節度使王行瑜侍中，佑國節度使張全義同平章事。

translations.literal: Bining military governor Wang Xingyu was promoted to Palace Attendant; Youguo military governor Zhang Quanyi was made Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingyu, military governor of Bining, was promoted to palace attendant; Zhang Quanyi, military governor of Youguo, was made co-director of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 官軍出陰地關，遊兵至於汾州。

translations.literal: The imperial armies exited Yindi Pass; roaming troops reached Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial armies marched out through Yindi Pass; advance parties reached Fenzhou.

sentences.zh: 李克用遣薛志勤、李承嗣將騎三千營於洪洞，李存孝將兵五千營於趙城。

translations.literal: Li Keyong sent Xue Zhiqin and Li Chengsi with three thousand horsemen to encamp at Hongdong, and Li Cunxiao with five thousand troops to encamp at Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong sent Xue Zhiqin and Li Chengsi with three thousand cavalry to camp at Hongdong and Li Cunxiao with five thousand men to camp at Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 鎮國節度使韓建以壯士三百夜襲存孝營，存孝知之，設伏以待之。

translations.literal: Zhenguo military governor Han Jian with three hundred stalwart men made a night raid on Cunxiao's camp; Cunxiao learned of it and set an ambush to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jian, military governor of Zhenguo, led three hundred picked men in a night attack on Cunxiao's camp; Cunxiao learned of it and laid an ambush.

sentences.zh: 建兵不利，靜難、鳳翔之兵不戰而走，禁軍自潰。

translations.literal: Jian's troops fared ill; the armies of Jingnan and Fengxiang fled without fighting; the palace guard army dissolved of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's troops were beaten; the Jingnan and Fengxiang forces fled without a fight; the palace guard collapsed on its own.

sentences.zh: 河東兵乘勝逐北，抵晉州西門。

translations.literal: The Hedong troops pursued the victory northward and reached the west gate of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The Hedong troops pursued and reached the west gate of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 張濬出戰，又敗，官軍死者近三千人。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun went out to battle and was again defeated; of the imperial armies nearly three thousand men died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun sallied forth and was beaten again; nearly three thousand imperial troops were killed.

sentences.zh: 靜難、鳳翔、保大、定難之軍先渡河西歸，濬獨有禁軍及宣武軍合萬人，與韓建閉城拒守，自是不敢復出。

translations.literal: The armies of Jingnan, Fengxiang, Baoda, and Dingnan first crossed the river west and returned; Jun alone had the palace guard and Xuanwu armies, ten thousand men in all, and with Han Jian shut the city and held it in defense; from then on he did not dare go out again.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingnan, Fengxiang, Baoda, and Dingnan armies crossed the Fen River westward and withdrew first; Jun was left with only the palace guard and Xuanwu troops, ten thousand men in all; he and Han Jian shut the gates and held the city, never daring to sally again.

sentences.zh: 存孝引兵攻絳州，十一月，刺史張行恭棄城走。

translations.literal: Cunxiao led troops to attack Jiang Prefecture; in the eleventh month the prefect Zhang Xinggong abandoned the city and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao marched on Jiangzhou; in the eleventh month Prefect Zhang Xinggong abandoned the city and fled.

sentences.zh: 存孝進攻晉州，三日，與其眾謀曰：「張濬宰相，俘之無益；

translations.literal: Cunxiao pressed the attack on Jin Prefecture; on the third day he consulted his masses, saying, "Zhang Jun is a chancellor—to capture him would be of no use;
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao pressed the siege of Jinzhou; on the third day he consulted his men: "Zhang Jun is a chancellor—capturing him would gain us nothing;

sentences.zh: 天子禁兵，不宜加害。」

translations.literal: the Son of Heaven's palace guard troops should not be harmed."
translations.idiomatic: the emperor's palace guard must not be harmed."

sentences.zh: 乃退五十里而軍；

translations.literal: Then he withdrew fifty li and encamped;
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew fifty li and made camp;

sentences.zh: 濬、建自含口遁去。

translations.literal: Jun and Jian stole away from Hankou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Jian slipped away from Hankou.

sentences.zh: 存孝取晉、絳二州，大掠慈、隰之境。

translations.literal: Cunxiao took Jin and Jiang prefectures and heavily plundered the territories of Ci and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxiao took Jin and Jiang and plundered Ci and Sui heavily.

sentences.zh: 先是，克用遣韓歸范歸朝，附表訟冤，言：「臣父子三代，受恩四朝，破龐勳，翦黃巢，黜襄王，存易定，致陛下今日冠通天之冠，佩白玉之璽，未必非臣之力也。

translations.literal: Earlier, Keyong had sent Han Guifan back to court with a memorial pleading injustice, saying, "Your servant's father and son for three generations received grace from four reigns; we broke Pang Xun, cut down Huang Chao, deposed the Prince of Xiang, preserved Yi and Ding, and enabled Your Majesty today to wear the cap reaching to Heaven and bear the white-jade seal—this was perhaps not without your servant's power.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Li Keyong had sent Han Guifan to court with a memorial of complaint, saying, "My father and I for three generations have served four reigns; we crushed Pang Xun, destroyed Huang Chao, deposed the Prince of Xiang, and preserved Yi and Ding—that Your Majesty today wears the cap of Heaven and the white-jade seal is surely no small part owing to my house.

sentences.zh: 若以攻雲州為臣罪，則拓跋思恭之取鄜延，朱全忠之侵徐、鄆，何獨不討？

translations.literal: If attacking Yun Prefecture is your servant's crime, then why were Tuoba Sigong's seizure of Fu and Yan and Zhu Quanzhong's encroachments on Xu and Yan alone not punished?
translations.idiomatic: If my crime is attacking Yunzhou, why were Tuoba Sigong's seizure of Fu-Yan and Zhu Quanzhong's raids on Xu and Yan not punished as well?

sentences.zh: 賞彼誅此，臣豈無辭！

translations.literal: To reward them and punish me—has your servant no argument!
translations.idiomatic: To reward them and punish me—do I have no case to make!

sentences.zh: 且朝廷當阽危之時，則譽臣為韓、彭、伊、呂；

translations.literal: Moreover, when the court was in peril, it praised your servant as Han, Peng, Yi, and Lü;
translations.idiomatic: When the court stood on the brink of ruin, it hailed me as Han Xin, Peng Yue, Yi Yin, and Lü Shang;

sentences.zh: 及既安之後，則罵臣為戎、羯、胡、夷。

translations.literal: once it was secure, it reviled your servant as Rong, Jie, Hu, and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: once danger passed, it reviled me as a barbarian, a foreigner, a Turk, a tribesman.

sentences.zh: 今天下握兵立功之人，獨不懼陛下它日之罵乎！

translations.literal: Today every man in the realm who holds troops and wins merit—is he alone not afraid of Your Majesty's reviling him some day!
translations.idiomatic: Surely every commander in the realm who holds troops and wins battles must fear the same reviling from Your Majesty one day!

sentences.zh: 況臣果有大罪，六師征之，自有典刑，何必幸臣之弱而後取之邪！

translations.literal: Moreover, if your servant truly had a great crime, the Six Armies would campaign against him and the statutory punishments would apply of themselves—why must you wait for your servant's weakness before taking him!
translations.idiomatic: If I truly had committed a grave crime, the imperial armies could march and the law would take its course—why wait until I was weak before moving against me!

sentences.zh: 今張濬既出帥，則固難束手，已集蕃、漢兵五十萬，欲直抵蒲、潼，與濬格鬥；

translations.literal: Now that Zhang Jun has already gone out as commander, it is indeed hard to submit passively; I have already gathered five hundred thousand barbarian and Han troops and wish to go straight to Pu and Tong to grapple with Jun;
translations.idiomatic: Now that Zhang Jun has taken command, I cannot simply yield; I have already assembled five hundred thousand barbarian and Han troops and mean to strike straight for Pu and Tong to fight Jun;

sentences.zh: 若其不勝，甘從削奪。

translations.literal: if I am not victorious, I am willing to accept stripping of rank.
translations.idiomatic: If I lose, I accept whatever stripping of rank the court decrees.

sentences.zh: 不然，方且輕騎叩閽，頓首丹陛，訴奸回於陛下之扆座，納制敕於先帝之廟庭，然後自拘司敗，恭俟鈇鍎。」

translations.literal: otherwise, I would shortly come with light cavalry to knock at the gate, bow my head on the cinnabar steps, plead against traitors and deceivers before Your Majesty's throne screen, deliver the edicts at the ancestral temple of the former emperor, and then confine myself to the judicial officer and respectfully await the axe."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise I would come with a light escort to the palace gate, prostrate myself before the throne, denounce the traitors at Your Majesty's seat, deliver my commission at the late emperor's temple, and then surrender myself to justice and await the executioner's axe."

sentences.zh: 表至，濬已敗，朝廷震恐。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, Jun had already been defeated, and the court was shaken with terror.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Jun had already been defeated, and the court was terrified.

sentences.zh: 濬與韓建逾王屋至河陽，撤民屋為筏以濟河，師徒失亡殆盡。

translations.literal: Jun and Han Jian crossed Wangwu to Heyang, tore down people's houses to make rafts to cross the river, and troops and followers were lost almost to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Han Jian crossed Wangwu to Heyang, tore down houses to build rafts to cross the river, and their army was nearly wiped out.

sentences.zh: 是役也，朝廷倚朱全忠及河朔三鎮；

translations.literal: In this campaign, the court relied on Zhu Quanzhong and the three circuits of Heshuo;
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign the court had counted on Zhu Quanzhong and the three Hebei circuits;

sentences.zh: 及濬至晉州，全忠方連兵徐、鄆，雖遣將攻澤州而身不至。

translations.literal: when Jun reached Jin Prefecture, Quanzhong was still linking troops at Xu and Yan; though he sent generals to attack Ze Prefecture, he himself did not come.
translations.idiomatic: when Jun reached Jinzhou, Quanzhong was still tied up in Xu and Yan; he sent generals against Zezhou but did not come in person.

sentences.zh: 行營乃求兵糧於鎮、魏，鎮、魏倚河東為扞蔽，皆不出兵；

translations.literal: The field headquarters then sought troops and grain from Zhen and Wei; Zhen and Wei relied on Hedong as a shield and sent out no troops;
translations.idiomatic: The campaign headquarters then asked Zhen and Wei for troops and grain; both circuits looked to Hedong as their shield and sent no troops;

sentences.zh: 惟華、邠、鳳翔、鄄、夏之兵會之。

translations.literal: only the troops of Hua, Bin, Fengxiang, Juan, and Xia joined them.
translations.idiomatic: Only troops from Hua, Bin, Fengxiang, Juan, and Xia joined the campaign.

sentences.zh: 兵未交而孫揆被擒，幽、雲俱敗，楊復恭復從中沮之，故濬軍望風自潰。

translations.literal: Before troops had engaged, Sun Kui was captured; of You and Yun both were defeated; Yang Fugong again obstructed from within—hence Jun's army collapsed at the mere sight of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Before a blow was struck Sun Kui was captured; the You and Yun forces were both defeated; Yang Fugong again sabotaged the effort from within—so Jun's army broke at the mere rumor of defeat.

sentences.zh: 十二月，己丑，孫儒拔蘇州，殺李友。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, on jichou, Sun Ru captured Su Prefecture and killed Li You.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on jichou, Sun Ru took Suzhou and killed Li You.

sentences.zh: 安仁義等聞之，焚潤廬舍，夜遁。

translations.literal: An Renyi and the others, hearing this, burned the buildings of Run and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: An Renyi and his men, hearing this, burned the buildings at Run and fled by night.

sentences.zh: 儒使沈粲守蘇州，又遣其將歸傳道守潤州。

translations.literal: Ru made Shen Can defend Su Prefecture, and also sent his general Gui Chuandao to defend Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ru put Shen Can in charge of Suzhou and sent his general Gui Chuandao to hold Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，汴將丁會、葛從周擊魏，渡河，取黎陽、臨河，龐師古、霍存下淇門、衛縣，朱全忠自以大軍繼之。

translations.literal: On xinchou, the Bian generals Ding Hui and Ge Congzhou attacked Wei, crossed the river, took Liyang and Linhe; Pang Shigu and Huo Cun reduced Qimen and Wei County; Zhu Quanzhong himself followed with a large army.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, the Bian generals Ding Hui and Ge Congzhou attacked Wei, crossed the river, and took Liyang and Linhe; Pang Shigu and Huo Cun seized Qimen and Wei County; Zhu Quanzhong followed in person with the main army.

sentences.zh: 是歲，置升州於上元縣，以張雄為刺史。

translations.literal: This year, Sheng Prefecture was established at Shangyuan County, with Zhang Xiong as its prefect.
translations.idiomatic: That year Shengzhou was created in Shangyuan County, with Zhang Xiong as prefect.

sentences.zh: 昭宗聖穆景文孝皇帝上之上大順二年（

translations.literal: Above, the second year of Dashun under Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, Glorious, Cultured, and Filial (
translations.idiomatic: Above: the second year of the Dashun era under Emperor Zhaozong the Sagely, Solemn, Glorious, Cultured, and Filial (

sentences.zh: 辛亥，公元八九一年）

translations.literal: xinhai, corresponding to the year 891 CE)
translations.idiomatic: xinhai, A.D. 891)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，羅弘信軍於內黃。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, Luo Hongxin encamped at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Luo Hongxin encamped at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，朱全忠擊之，五戰皆捷，到永定橋，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Zhu Quanzhong attacked him; in five battles all were victories; reaching Yongding Bridge, heads cut numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Zhu Quanzhong attacked him, won five battles in succession, and at Yongding Bridge took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 弘信懼，遣使厚幣請和。

translations.literal: Hongxin feared, sent envoys with generous gifts to sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Hongxin sent envoys bearing lavish gifts to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 全忠命止焚掠，歸其俘，還軍河上。

translations.literal: Quanzhong ordered that burning and plunder cease, their captives be returned, and the army withdraw to the river's bank.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong ordered his men to stop burning and looting, returned the prisoners, and withdrew to the north bank of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 魏博自是服於汴。

translations.literal: Weibo from this submitted to Bian.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Weibo submitted to Bian.

sentences.zh: 庚申，制以太保、門下侍郎、同平章事孔緯為荊南節度使，中書侍郎、同平章事張濬為鄂岳觀察使。

translations.literal: On gengshen, by decree Grand Tutor, Vice Director of the Secretariat, and Co-Director of the Secretariat-Chancellery Kong Wei was made military governor of Jingnan; Vice Director of the Chancellery and Co-Director Zhang Jun was made governor of E-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen an edict appointed Grand Tutor and Co-Director Kong Wei military governor of Jingnan, and Co-Director Zhang Jun governor of E-Yue.

sentences.zh: 以翰林學士承旨、兵部侍郎崔昭緯同平章事，御史中丞徐彥若為戶部侍郎、同平章事，昭緯，慎由從子；

translations.literal: The Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy and Vice Minister of War Cui Zhaowei was made Co-Director; the Censor-in-Chief Xu Yanzuo was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Co-Director; Zhaowei was a nephew of Shen You;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhaowei, Academician Expositor-in-Chief of the Hanlin Academy and Vice Minister of War, was made Co-Director; Xu Yanzuo, Censor-in-Chief, was made Vice Minister of Revenue and Co-Director; Zhaowei was a nephew of Shen You;

sentences.zh: 彥若，商之子也。

translations.literal: Yanzuo was a son of Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzuo was the son of Shang.

sentences.zh: 楊復恭使人劫孔緯於長樂坡，斬其旌節，資裝俱盡，緯僅能自免。

translations.literal: Yang Fugong sent men to waylay Kong Wei at Changle Slope, cut down his insignia of office, and stripped all his goods and baggage; Wei barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong's agents ambushed Kong Wei at Changle Slope, destroyed his banners of office, and seized all his baggage; Wei barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 李克用復遣使上表曰：「張濬以陛下萬代之業，邀自己一時之功，知臣與朱溫深仇，私相連結。

translations.literal: Li Keyong again sent an envoy with a memorial saying: "Zhang Jun, in the name of Your Majesty's enterprise for ten thousand generations, sought his own glory for a single moment; knowing that your subject and Zhu Wen were deep foes, privately joined with him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong again memorialized the throne: "Zhang Jun wagered Your Majesty's long-term interests for his own momentary triumph; knowing that I am Zhu Wen's bitter enemy, he colluded with him in secret.

sentences.zh: 臣今身無官爵，名是罪人，不敢歸陛下籓方，且欲於河中寄寓，進退行止，伏俟指麾。」

translations.literal: Your subject now has no office or rank, and my name marks me as a criminal; I dare not return to Your Majesty's frontier domains, and wish only to lodge temporarily at Hezhong; in advance or retreat, movement or rest, I await your commands prostrate."
translations.idiomatic: I now hold no rank and stand condemned as a criminal; I dare not return to the frontier on Your Majesty's behalf, and wish only to take refuge at Hezhong until I receive your orders."

sentences.zh: 詔再貶孔緯均州刺史，張濬連州刺史。

translations.literal: By edict Kong Wei was again demoted to prefect of Jun Prefecture, and Zhang Jun to prefect of Lian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An edict further demoted Kong Wei to prefect of Junzhou and Zhang Jun to prefect of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 賜克用詔，悉復其官爵，使歸晉陽。

translations.literal: Keyong was granted an edict fully restoring all his offices and titles, and was ordered to return to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong received an edict restoring all his ranks and titles and ordering him back to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 孫儒盡舉淮、蔡之兵濟江，癸酉，自潤州轉戰而南，田頵、安仁義屢敗退，楊行密城戍皆望風奔潰。

translations.literal: Sun Ru mustered all the troops of Huai and Cai to cross the river; on guiyou, from Run Prefecture he fought southward in succession; Tian Yun and An Renyi were repeatedly defeated and driven back; the garrisons of Yang Xingmi all fled at the mere sight of the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru mustered every soldier of Huai and Cai and crossed the Yangtze; on guiyou he fought south from Runzhou; Tian Yun and An Renyi were repeatedly beaten back, and Yang Xingmi's garrisons collapsed at the first rumor of his approach.

sentences.zh: 儒將李從立奄至宣州東溪，行密守備尚未固，眾心危懼，夜，使其將合肥台濛將五百人屯溪西；

translations.literal: Ru's general Li Congli suddenly arrived at the East Stream of Xuan Prefecture; Xingmi's defenses were not yet secure, and hearts were fearful; by night he had his general Tai Meng of Hefei lead five hundred men to encamp west of the stream;
translations.idiomatic: Ru's general Li Congli suddenly reached the East Stream outside Xuanzhou; Xingmi's defenses were not yet firm and morale was shaken; that night he sent his general Tai Meng of Hefei with five hundred men to camp west of the stream;

sentences.zh: 濛使士卒傳呼，往返數四，從立以為大眾繼至，遽引去。

translations.literal: Meng had soldiers call out back and forth four or five times; Congli thought a large force was coming and hurriedly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Meng had his men shout back and forth four or five times; Congli took this for the vanguard of a large army and withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 儒前軍至溧水，行密使都指揮使李神福拒之。

translations.literal: Ru's vanguard reached Lishui; Xingmi sent the chief commander Li Shenfu to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Ru's vanguard reached Lishui; Xingmi sent his chief commander Li Shenfu to block them.

sentences.zh: 神福陽退以示怯，儒軍不設備，神福夜帥精兵襲之，俘斬千人。

translations.literal: Shenfu feigned retreat to show cowardice; Ru's army took no precautions; Shenfu by night led elite troops in a raid, capturing and killing a thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu feigned retreat to appear timid; Ru's army lowered its guard; Shenfu led picked troops in a night attack and killed or captured a thousand men.

sentences.zh: 二月，加李克用守中書令，復李罕之官爵；

translations.literal: Second month, Li Keyong was given the acting appointment of Director of the Secretariat; Li Hanzhi's offices and titles were restored;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Li Keyong was made acting Director of the Secretariat, and Li Hanzhi's offices and titles were restored;

sentences.zh: 再貶張濬繡州司戶。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun was again demoted to registrar of Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun was again demoted to registrar of Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 韋昭度將諸道兵十餘萬討陳敬瑄，三年不能克，饋運不繼，朝議欲息兵。

translations.literal: Wei Zhaodu led over one hundred thousand troops from the various circuits against Chen Jingxuan; for three years he could not conquer; supply transport could not be sustained; court discussion wished to cease hostilities.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhaodu had led more than a hundred thousand troops from the various circuits against Chen Jingxuan; after three years he still could not take the city, supplies ran out, and the court debated calling off the campaign.

sentences.zh: 三月，乙亥，制復敬瑄官爵，令顧彥朗、王建各帥眾歸鎮。

translations.literal: Third month, on yihai, by decree Jingxuan's offices and titles were restored, and Gu Yanlang and Wang Jian were each ordered to lead their troops back to their jurisdictions.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on yihai, an edict restored Jingxuan's offices and titles and ordered Gu Yanlang and Wang Jian each to lead their forces back to their posts.

sentences.zh: 王師範遣都指揮使盧弘擊攻棣州刺史張蟾，弘引兵還攻師池，師範使人以重賂迎之，曰：「師範童騃，不堪重任，願得避位，使保首領，公之仁也。」

translations.literal: Wang Shifan sent Chief Commander Lu Hong to attack and assault Zhang Chan, prefect of Di Prefecture; Hong led troops back to attack Shichi; Shifan sent someone with heavy bribes to greet him, saying: "Shifan is childish and foolish, unfit for heavy responsibility; I wish to yield my place so that I may keep my head—that would be your kindness."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shifan sent his chief commander Lu Hong to attack Zhang Chan, prefect of Dizhou; Hong turned back to assault Shifan's base; Shifan sent an envoy with lavish bribes, saying: "Shifan is young and unfit for command; I wish to step aside and keep my head—that would be an act of mercy on your part."

sentences.zh: 弘以師範年少，信之，不設備。

translations.literal: Hong, seeing Shifan was young, believed him and took no precautions.
translations.idiomatic: Hong, thinking Shifan was merely a boy, believed him and let down his guard.

sentences.zh: 師範密謂小校安丘劉鄩曰：「汝能殺弘，吾以汝為大將。」

translations.literal: Shifan secretly said to the junior officer Liu Yun of Anqiu: "If you can kill Hong, I will make you chief general."
translations.idiomatic: Shifan secretly told the junior officer Liu Yun of Anqiu: "If you kill Hong, I will make you chief general."

sentences.zh: 弘入城，師範伏甲而享之，鄩殺弘於座及其黨數人。

translations.literal: When Hong entered the city, Shifan set armed men in ambush and feasted him; Yun killed Hong at table along with several of his partisans.
translations.idiomatic: When Hong entered the city, Shifan hid armed men and entertained him at a feast; Yun killed Hong at table along with several of his followers.

sentences.zh: 師範慰諭士卒，厚賞重誓，自將以攻棣州，執張蟾，斬之。

translations.literal: Shifan comforted and instructed the soldiers, gave lavish rewards and solemn oaths, and personally led an attack on Di Prefecture, seized Zhang Chan, and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan rallied the troops with generous rewards and solemn pledges, then personally led the assault on Dizhou, captured Zhang Chan, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 崔安潛逃歸京師。

translations.literal: Cui Anqian fled and returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Anqian fled back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 師範以鄩為馬步副都指揮使。

translations.literal: Shifan made Yun deputy chief commander of horse and foot.
translations.idiomatic: Shifan appointed Yun deputy chief commander of horse and foot.

sentences.zh: 詔以師範為平盧節度使。

translations.literal: By edict Shifan was made military governor of Pinglu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Shifan military governor of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 師範和謹好學，每本縣令到官，師範輒備儀衛往謁之；

translations.literal: Shifan was mild, careful, and fond of learning; whenever a new county magistrate of his home county took office, Shifan would prepare escort and guards to go pay a visit;
translations.idiomatic: Shifan was courteous, diligent, and fond of learning; whenever a new magistrate arrived in his home county, he would go to pay his respects with a full escort;

sentences.zh: 令不敢當，師範命客將挾持，令坐於聽事，自稱「百姓王師範」，拜之於庭。

translations.literal: The magistrate dared not accept this; Shifan ordered his guest officer to support him and make him sit in the hall of audience; Shifan called himself "the commoner Wang Shifan" and bowed to him in the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate protested that this was improper; Shifan had his usher support him and seat him in the hall of audience, then called himself "the commoner Wang Shifan" and bowed to him in the courtyard.

sentences.zh: 僚佐或諫，師範曰：「吾敬桑梓，所以教子孫不忘本也。」

translations.literal: A subordinate sometimes remonstrated; Shifan said: "I respect my native place—this is to teach my descendants not to forget their roots."
translations.idiomatic: When his staff remonstrated, Shifan said: "I honor my native place so that my descendants will never forget where they came from."

sentences.zh: 張濬至藍田，逃奔華州依韓建，與孔緯密求救於朱全忠。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun reached Lantian, fled to Hua Prefecture and relied on Han Jian, and with Kong Wei secretly sought rescue from Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun reached Lantian, fled to Huazhou and took refuge with Han Jian, and together with Kong Wei secretly appealed to Zhu Quanzhong for help.

sentences.zh: 全忠上表為緯、濬訟冤，朝廷不得已，並聽自便。

translations.literal: Quanzhong submitted a memorial pleading the grievances of Wei and Jun; the court had no choice but to let both do as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong memorialized the throne on behalf of Wei and Jun; the court, left with no alternative, allowed both men to go where they wished.

sentences.zh: 緯至商州而還，亦寓居華州。

translations.literal: Wei reached Shang Prefecture and returned, and also took lodging at Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wei went as far as Shangzhou and turned back, and also took up residence at Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 邢洺節度使安知建潛通朱全忠，李克用表以李存孝代之。

translations.literal: The military governor of Xing-Ming, An Zhijian, secretly communicated with Zhu Quanzhong; Li Keyong memorialized that Li Cunxiao replace him.
translations.idiomatic: An Zhijian, military governor of Xing-Ming, was secretly in contact with Zhu Quanzhong; Li Keyong memorialized that Li Cunxiao replace him.

sentences.zh: 知建懼，奔青州，朝廷以知建為神武統軍。

translations.literal: Zhijian feared, fled to Qing Prefecture; the court made Zhijian commander-in-chief of Shenwu.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Zhijian fled to Qingzhou; the court appointed him commander-in-chief of Shenwu.

sentences.zh: 知建帥麾下三千人將詣京師，過鄆州。

translations.literal: Zhijian led three thousand men under his command intending to go to the capital, passing through Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijian set out for the capital with three thousand men under his command, passing through Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 朱瑄與克用方睦，伏兵河上，斬之，傳首晉陽。

translations.literal: Zhu Xuan was then on good terms with Keyong; he set an ambush on the river, executed him, and sent the head to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Xuan was then allied with Keyong; he laid an ambush on the riverbank, killed Zhijian, and sent his head to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，有彗星見於三台，東行入太微，長十丈餘。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, a comet appeared at Santai, traveled east into Taiwei, more than ten zhang in length.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fourth month, a comet appeared at Santai, moved east into Taiwei, and stretched more than ten zhang long.

sentences.zh: 甲申，赦天下。

translations.literal: On jiashen, amnesty for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, an amnesty was proclaimed for all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 成都城中乏食，棄兒滿路。

translations.literal: Within Chengdu city food was scarce; abandoned children filled the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Food ran short inside Chengdu, and abandoned children lined the streets.

sentences.zh: 民有潛入行營販米入城者，邏者得之，以白韋昭度，昭度曰：「滿城饑甚，忍不救之！」

translations.literal: There were civilians who secretly entered the camp to sell rice in the city; patrols caught them and reported to Wei Zhaodu; Zhaodu said: "The whole city is starving terribly—how can we bear not to save them!"
translations.idiomatic: Some civilians had been slipping into the camp to sell rice in the city; patrols caught them and reported to Wei Zhaodu, who said: "The whole city is starving—how can we refuse to help them!"

sentences.zh: 釋勿問。

translations.literal: They were released and no inquiry was made.
translations.idiomatic: They were released without punishment.

sentences.zh: 亦有白陳敬瑄者，敬瑄曰：「吾恨無術以救餓者，彼能如是，勿禁也。」

translations.literal: Some also reported to Chen Jingxuan; Jingxuan said: "I regret that I have no means to save the starving; if they can do this, do not forbid it."
translations.idiomatic: Others reported the matter to Chen Jingxuan, who said: "I have no way to save the starving myself; if people can do this, do not stop them."

sentences.zh: 由是販者浸多，然所致不過斗升，截筒，逕寸半，深五分，量米而鬻之，每筒百餘錢，餓殍狼籍。

translations.literal: From this sellers gradually increased, but what they brought was no more than a few pints; they used cut bamboo tubes, one and a half inches in diameter and five fen deep, to measure and sell rice; each tube sold for more than a hundred cash; corpses of the starved lay strewn about.
translations.idiomatic: Sellers soon multiplied, but each brought only a pint or two, measured out in cut bamboo tubes an inch and a half across and five fen deep; each tube fetched more than a hundred cash, while corpses of the starved lay everywhere.

sentences.zh: 軍民強弱相陵，將吏斬之不能禁；

translations.literal: Soldiers and civilians, strong and weak, preyed on one another; officers and clerks executed offenders but could not stop it;
translations.idiomatic: Strong preyed on weak among soldiers and civilians alike; officers executed offenders but could not stop it;

sentences.zh: 乃更為酷法，或斷腰，或斜劈，死者相繼而為者不止。

translations.literal: they then made even harsher punishments—some cut at the waist, some slashed diagonally; the dead followed one another but those who did it did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: they then imposed crueler penalties—some were cut in two at the waist, others hacked diagonally; the dead piled up, yet the crimes continued.

sentences.zh: 人耳目既熟，不以為懼。

translations.literal: People's eyes and ears had grown accustomed, and they did not regard it with fear.
translations.idiomatic: People grew so used to the sight that they no longer feared it.

sentences.zh: 吏民日窘，多謀出降，敬瑄悉捕其族黨殺之，慘毒備至。

translations.literal: Officials and civilians grew daily more desperate; many plotted to surrender; Jingxuan seized all their clans and associates and killed them, cruelty in full measure.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and civilians grew more desperate by the day; many plotted to surrender; Jingxuan arrested their entire clans and associates and killed them with every cruelty imaginable.

sentences.zh: 內外都指揮使、眉州刺史成都徐耕，性仁恕，所全活數千人。

translations.literal: The chief commander for inner and outer defense, Xu Geng of Chengdu, prefect of Meizhou, was by nature benevolent and forgiving; those he spared numbered several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Geng of Chengdu, chief commander for inner and outer defense and prefect of Meizhou, was by nature merciful; he spared several thousand lives.

sentences.zh: 田令孜曰：「公掌生殺而不刑一人，有異志邪？」

translations.literal: Tian Lingzi said: "You hold the power of life and death yet punish not a single person—have you a rebellious mind?"
translations.idiomatic: Tian Lingzi said: "You hold the power of life and death yet execute no one—do you harbor rebellious intentions?"

sentences.zh: 耕懼，夜，取俘囚戮於市。

translations.literal: Geng feared; by night he took prisoners and executed them in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Geng was terrified; that night he took prisoners and executed them in the market.

sentences.zh: 王建見罷兵制書，曰：「大功垂成，奈何棄之！」

translations.literal: Wang Jian saw the edict ceasing hostilities and said: "Great success is about to be achieved—how can we abandon it!"
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Jian saw the edict ordering the army to stand down, he said: "Victory is within reach—how can we throw it away!"

sentences.zh: 謀於周庠，庠勸建請韋公還朝，獨攻成都，克而有之。

translations.literal: He consulted Zhou Xu; Xu urged Jian to ask Duke Wei to return to court, attack Chengdu alone, and take it by conquest.
translations.idiomatic: He consulted Zhou Xu, who urged Jian to ask Duke Wei to return to court while Jian alone besieged and captured Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 建表稱：「陳敬瑄、田令孜罪不可赦，願畢命以圖成功。」

translations.literal: Jian submitted a memorial saying: "Chen Jingxuan and Tian Lingzi are guilty beyond pardon; I wish to spend my life to achieve success."
translations.idiomatic: Jian memorialized the throne: "Chen Jingxuan and Tian Lingzi are guilty beyond pardon; I am willing to stake my life on finishing the campaign."

sentences.zh: 昭度無如之何，由是未能東還。

translations.literal: Zhaodu could do nothing about it; from this he was unable to return east.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu could not refuse, and from that point he was unable to return east.

sentences.zh: 建說昭度曰：「今關東籓鎮迭相吞噬，此腹心之疾也，相公宜早歸廟堂，與天子謀之。

translations.literal: Jian advised Zhaodu, saying: "Now the frontier domains east of the passes devour one another in succession—this is a disease of the heart and belly; the lord minister should early return to the court and consult with the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Jian urged Zhaodu: "The eastern circuits are devouring one another—this is a mortal threat to the throne; you should return to court at once and counsel the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄，疥癬耳，當以日月制之，責建，可辦也！」

translations.literal: Jingxuan is but scabies and ringworm; he should be controlled in the time of sun and moon; charge Jian, and it can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan is a mere skin rash; given time he can be contained—leave him to Jian, and the job can be done!"

sentences.zh: 昭度猶豫未決。

translations.literal: Zhaodu hesitated and could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu wavered and could not make up his mind.

sentences.zh: 庚子，建陰令東川將唐友通等擒昭度親吏駱保於行府門，臠食之，雲其盜軍糧。

translations.literal: On gengzi, Jian secretly had the Dongchuan generals Tang Youtong and others seize Zhaodu's intimate clerk Luo Bao at the campaign headquarters gate, dismember and eat him, claiming he had stolen army grain.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, Jian secretly had the Dongchuan generals Tang Youtong and others seize Zhaodu's personal clerk Luo Bao at the campaign headquarters gate, butcher and eat him, claiming he had stolen army grain.

sentences.zh: 昭度大懼，遽稱疾，以印節授建，牒建知三使留後兼行營招討使，即日東還。

translations.literal: Zhaodu was greatly afraid, hurriedly claimed illness, handed his seal and baton to Jian, issued a dispatch making Jian acting commissioner of the three envoys and concurrently campaign pacification commissioner, and returned east the same day.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaodu was terrified; he at once pleaded illness, handed his seal and baton to Jian, issued orders making Jian acting commissioner of the three envoys and campaign pacification commissioner, and returned east the same day.

sentences.zh: 建送至新都，跪觴馬前，泣拜而別。

translations.literal: Jian escorted him to Xindu, knelt with wine before his horse, wept and bowed in parting.
translations.idiomatic: Jian escorted him to Xindu, knelt with a cup of wine before his horse, and wept as he bowed farewell.

sentences.zh: 昭度甫出劍門，即以兵守之，不復內東軍。

translations.literal: Zhaodu had barely left Jianmen when Jian at once posted troops to guard it, and no longer admitted eastern troops within.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had Zhaodu passed through Jianmen when Jian posted troops to hold the pass and barred all eastern forces from entering.

sentences.zh: 昭度至京師，除東都留守。

translations.literal: Zhaodu reached the capital and was appointed guardian of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaodu reached the capital, he was appointed guardian of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 建急攻成都，環城烽塹亙五十里。

translations.literal: Jian pressed the attack on Chengdu urgently; signal fires and trenches ringed the city for fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: Jian pressed the siege of Chengdu; beacon fires and trenches stretched fifty li around the walls.

sentences.zh: 有狗屠王鷂，請詐得罪亡入城說之，使上下離心，建遣之。

translations.literal: There was a dog butcher, Wang Yao, who asked to feign offense, flee into the city, and persuade them, so that superiors and subordinates would lose heart; Jian sent him.
translations.idiomatic: A dog butcher named Wang Yao volunteered to pretend he had committed a crime, flee into the city, and sow discord; Jian sent him in.

sentences.zh: 鷂入見陳敬瑄、田令孜，則言「建兵疲食盡，將遁矣」，出則鬻茶於市，陰為吏民稱建英武，兵勢強盛；

translations.literal: Yao entered and saw Chen Jingxuan and Tian Lingzi, and then said "Jian's troops are weary and food is spent—they are about to flee"; going out he sold tea in the market, secretly speaking for officials and civilians to praise Jian's martial prowess and the strength of his army;
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city Yao told Chen Jingxuan and Tian Lingzi that Jian's army was exhausted and starving and about to withdraw; outside he sold tea in the market and quietly praised Jian's martial prowess and the strength of his forces;

sentences.zh: 由是敬瑄等懈於守備而眾心危懼。

translations.literal: from this Jingxuan and the others slackened in defense while popular hearts were fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan and his men slackened their defenses, while the populace grew fearful and unsettled.

sentences.zh: 建又遣其將京兆鄭渥詐降以覘之，敬瑄以為將，使乘城，既而復以詐得歸。

translations.literal: Jian also sent his general Zheng Wo of Jingzhao to feign surrender and spy; Jingxuan made him a general and had him mount the wall; afterward he again by deception obtained his return.
translations.idiomatic: Jian also sent his general Zheng Wo of Jingzhao to feign surrender and spy on the city; Jingxuan made him a commander and put him on the walls; later Wo slipped out by the same ruse.

sentences.zh: 建由是悉知城中虛實，以渥為親從都指揮使，更姓名曰王宗渥。

translations.literal: "Jian from this fully knew the situation inside the city; he made Wo chief personal commander and changed his name to Wang Zongwo."
translations.idiomatic: "Jian thus learned the city's every weakness; he made Wo chief personal commander and renamed him Wang Zongwo."

sentences.zh: 以武安節度使周岳為嶺南西道節度使。

translations.literal: The military governor of Wu'an, Zhou Yue, was made military governor of Lingnan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yue, military governor of Wu'an, was appointed military governor of Lingnan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 李克用大舉擊赫連鐸，敗其兵於河上，進圍雲州。

translations.literal: Li Keyong launched a major attack on Helian Duo, defeated his army on the river, and advanced to besiege Yun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong launched a major campaign against Helian Duo, routed his army on the river, and advanced to besiege Yunzhou.

sentences.zh: 楊行密遣其將劉威、朱延壽將兵三萬擊孫儒於黃池，威等大敗。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent his generals Liu Wei and Zhu Yanshou to lead thirty thousand troops to attack Sun Ru at Huangchi; Wei and the others suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent his generals Liu Wei and Zhu Yanshou with thirty thousand men against Sun Ru at Huangchi; they were routed.

sentences.zh: 延壽，舒城人也。

translations.literal: Yanshou was a man of Shucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou was a native of Shucheng.

sentences.zh: 孫儒軍於黃池，五月，大水，諸營皆沒，乃還揚州，使其將康暀據和州，安景思據滁州。

translations.literal: Sun Ru encamped at Huangchi; in the fifth month great floods came and all camps were submerged; he then returned to Yang Prefecture and had his generals Kang Wei hold He Prefecture and An Jingsi hold Chu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru was encamped at Huangchi; in the fifth month a great flood submerged every camp, so he withdrew to Yangzhou and left his generals Kang Wei at Hezhou and An Jingsi at Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙午，立皇子祐為德王。

translations.literal: On bingwu, the imperial prince You was established as Prince De.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, the imperial prince You was created Prince De.

sentences.zh: 楊行密遣其將李神福攻和、滁，康暀降，安景思走。

translations.literal: Yang Xingmi sent his general Li Shenfu to attack He and Chu; Kang Wei surrendered and An Jingsi fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi sent Li Shenfu against Hezhou and Chuzhou; Kang Wei surrendered and An Jingsi fled.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，李克用急攻雲州，赫連鐸食盡，奔吐谷渾部，既而歸於幽州。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Li Keyong pressed the attack on Yun Prefecture urgently; Helian Duo exhausted his food, fled to the Tuyuhun tribes, and afterward returned to You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Li Keyong pressed the siege of Yunzhou; Helian Duo ran out of food, fled to the Tuyuhun, and later made his way to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 克用表大將石善友為大同防禦使。

translations.literal: Keyong memorialized that the great general Shi Shanyou be made defense commissioner of Datong.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong memorialized that his great general Shi Shanyou be appointed defense commissioner of Datong.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣使與楊行密約共攻孫儒。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent envoys to agree with Yang Xingmi on a joint attack on Sun Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent envoys to Yang Xingmi proposing a joint attack on Sun Ru.

sentences.zh: 儒恃其兵強，欲先滅行密，後敵全忠，移牒籓鎮，數行密、全忠之罪，且曰：「俟平宣、汴，當引兵入朝，除君側之惡。」

translations.literal: Ru relied on the strength of his troops, wished first to destroy Xingmi and afterward oppose Quanzhong; he sent dispatches to the frontier domains enumerating the crimes of Xingmi and Quanzhong, and said: "When Xuan and Bian are pacified, I shall lead troops to court and remove evil beside the sovereign."
translations.idiomatic: Ru, confident in his strength, planned first to destroy Xingmi and then turn on Quanzhong; he sent dispatches to the circuits denouncing Xingmi and Quanzhong, declaring: "Once Xuan and Bian are pacified, I shall march to court and purge the evil at the sovereign's side."

sentences.zh: 於是悉焚揚州廬舍，盡驅丁壯及婦女渡江，殺老弱以充食。

translations.literal: Thereupon he burned all the buildings of Yang Prefecture, drove all able-bodied men and women to cross the river, and killed the old and weak to serve as food.
translations.idiomatic: He then burned every building in Yangzhou, drove all able-bodied men and women across the river, and killed the old and weak for food.

sentences.zh: 行密將張訓、李德誠潛入揚州，滅餘火，得谷數十萬斛以賑饑民。

translations.literal: Xingmi's generals Zhang Xun and Li Decheng secretly entered Yang Prefecture, extinguished the remaining fires, and obtained several hundred thousand hu of grain to relieve the starving people.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi's generals Zhang Xun and Li Decheng slipped into Yangzhou, put out the remaining fires, and recovered several hundred thousand hu of grain to feed the starving.

sentences.zh: 泗州刺史張諫貸數萬斛以給軍，訓以行密之命饋之，諫由是德行密。

translations.literal: The prefect of Si Prefecture, Zhang Jian, loaned several ten thousand hu to supply the army; Xun, on Xingmi's orders, sent it as provisions; Jian from this accorded virtue to Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jian, prefect of Sizhou, had loaned tens of thousands of hu to supply the army; Xun, on Xingmi's orders, returned the grain as provisions; Jian thereafter held Xingmi in high regard.

sentences.zh: 邢洺節度使李存孝勸李克用攻鎮州，克用從之。

translations.literal: The military governor of Xing-Ming, Li Cunxiao, urged Li Keyong to attack Zhen Prefecture; Keyong agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunxiao, military governor of Xing-Ming, urged Li Keyong to attack Zhenzhou; Keyong agreed.

sentences.zh: 八月，克用南巡澤潞，遂涉懷孟之境。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Keyong toured south through Ze and Lu, and then crossed into the territory of Huai and Meng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Keyong marched south through Ze and Lu and entered the territory of Huai and Meng.

sentences.zh: 朱全忠遣其將丁會攻宿州，克其外城。

translations.literal: Zhu Quanzhong sent his general Ding Hui to attack Su Prefecture and captured its outer city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong sent Ding Hui to attack Suzhou and captured the outer city.

sentences.zh: 乙未，孫儒自蘇州出屯廣德，楊行密引兵拒之。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Sun Ru came out from Su Prefecture and encamped at Guangde; Yang Xingmi led troops to oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Sun Ru marched out from Suzhou and encamped at Guangde; Yang Xingmi led troops to block him.

sentences.zh: 儒圍其寨，行密將上蔡李簡帥百餘人力戰，破寨，拔行密出之。

translations.literal: Ru besieged his camp; Xingmi's general Li Jian of Shangcai led more than a hundred men in fierce fighting, broke the camp, and pulled Xingmi out of it.
translations.idiomatic: Ru besieged Xingmi's camp; Xingmi's general Li Jian of Shangcai led a hundred-odd men in a desperate fight, broke the encirclement, and rescued Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 王建攻陳敬瑄益急，敬瑄出戰輒敗，巡內州縣率為建所取。

translations.literal: Wang Jian's attack on Chen Jingxuan grew ever more urgent; Jingxuan came out to battle and was repeatedly defeated; the prefectures and counties within the circuit were one after another taken by Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian's assault on Chen Jingxuan grew fiercer; Jingxuan sallied forth and was beaten every time; prefecture after prefecture within the circuit fell to Jian.

sentences.zh: 威戎節度使楊晟時饋之食，建以兵據新都，彭州道絕。

translations.literal: The military governor of Weirong, Yang Sheng, periodically supplied Jingxuan with food; Jian with troops held Xindu, and the route to Peng Prefecture was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sheng, military governor of Weirong, had been sending food to Jingxuan; Jian seized Xindu with troops and cut the road to Pengzhou.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄出，慰勉士卒，皆不應。

translations.literal: Jingxuan came out, comforted and exhorted the soldiers, and none responded.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan came out to rally the troops, but not a man answered.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，田令孜登城謂建曰：「老夫向於公甚厚，何見困如是？」

translations.literal: On xinchou, Tian Lingze mounted the wall and said to Jian, "This old man was ever very kind to you—why are you pressing me so?"
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou, Tian Lingze went up on the wall and said to Wang Jian, "I have always treated you generously—why must you corner me like this?"

sentences.zh: 建曰：「父子之恩豈敢忘！

translations.literal: Jian said, "How could I dare forget the kindness between father and son!
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian replied, "I would never forget the bond between us, as between father and son!

sentences.zh: 但朝廷命建討不受代者，不得不然。

translations.literal: But the court has ordered Jian to punish one who refuses transfer of office—I cannot do otherwise.
translations.idiomatic: But the court commanded me to suppress a man who refuses to yield his post; I had no choice.

sentences.zh: 倘太師改圖，建復何求！」

translations.literal: If the Grand Preceptor would change his course, what more would Jian ask!"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Grace will reconsider, what more could I want!"

sentences.zh: 是夕，令孜自攜西川印節詣建營授之，將士皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: That evening, Lingze himself took the seal and insignia of Xichuan and went to Jian's camp to hand them over; officers and soldiers all shouted "Long live!"
translations.idiomatic: That night Tian Lingze brought the seal and regalia of the Xichuan command himself to Wang Jian's camp and surrendered them; the troops burst into cheers of "Long live the Emperor!"

sentences.zh: 建泣謝，請復為父子如初。

translations.literal: Jian wept and thanked him, asking that they be father and son again as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian wept his thanks and asked that their bond be restored as before.

sentences.zh: 先是，建常誘其將士曰：「成都城中繁盛如花錦，一朝得之，金帛子女恣汝曹所取，節度使與汝曹迭日為之耳！」

translations.literal: Earlier, Jian had often incited his officers and soldiers, saying, "Within Chengdu the city flourishes like brocaded flowers; once it is taken in a morning, gold, silk, women, and children—you may take as you please; the military governorship will be yours by turns, day after day!"
translations.idiomatic: Before this, Wang Jian had repeatedly tempted his troops with promises: "Chengdu blooms like brocade and embroidery; seize it in a single morning and gold, silk, women, and children are yours for the taking—you'll take turns serving as military governor, one day each!"

sentences.zh: 壬寅，敬瑄開城迎建。

translations.literal: On renyin, Jingxuan opened the city and welcomed Jian in.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin, Chen Jingxuan opened the gates and welcomed Wang Jian inside.

sentences.zh: 建署其將張勍為馬步斬斫使，使先入城。

translations.literal: Jian appointed his general Zhang Qin as commissioner of cavalry and infantry execution and cutting, and had him enter the city first.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian named his general Zhang Qin marshal of cavalry and infantry executioners and sent him into the city ahead of the rest.

sentences.zh: 乃謂將士曰：「吾與汝曹三年百戰，今始得城，汝曹不憂不富忠，慎勿焚掠坊市。

translations.literal: He then said to the officers and soldiers, "I and you have fought a hundred battles these three years; only now have we taken the city—you need not worry about lacking wealth; take care not to burn and plunder the wards and markets.
translations.idiomatic: Then he addressed the troops: "We have fought a hundred battles these three years, and only now have we won the city. You will not lack for riches—but do not burn or loot the streets and markets.

sentences.zh: 吾已委張勍護之矣，彼幸執而白我，我猶得赦之；

translations.literal: I have already entrusted Zhang Qin to keep order; if he captures you and reports to me, I may still pardon you;
translations.idiomatic: I have put Zhang Qin in charge of enforcement; if he catches you and reports it to me first, I may still spare you—

sentences.zh: 若先斬而後白，吾亦不能救也！」

translations.literal: if you are beheaded first and reported afterward, I also cannot save you!"
translations.idiomatic: but if he beheads you first and reports afterward, even I cannot save you!"

sentences.zh: 既而士卒有犯令者，勍執百餘人，皆捶其胸而殺之，積屍於市，眾莫敢犯。

translations.literal: Before long, soldiers who violated the order were seized by Qin—more than a hundred men; all were beaten on the chest and killed; corpses piled up in the market, and none dared offend.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward soldiers broke the rules; Zhang Qin seized more than a hundred of them, beat them to death by smashing their chests, and piled the bodies in the marketplace until no one dared violate the order.

sentences.zh: 故時人謂勍為「張打胸」。

translations.literal: Hence men of the time called Qin "Zhang Chest-Beater."
translations.idiomatic: People nicknamed him "Zhang Chest-Pounder."

sentences.zh: 癸卯，建入城，自稱西川留後。

translations.literal: On guimao, Jian entered the city and styled himself acting governor of Xichuan.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Wang Jian entered the city and proclaimed himself acting military governor of Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 小校韓武數於使廳上馬，牙司止之，武怒曰：「司徒許我迭日為節度使；

translations.literal: The junior officer Han Wu repeatedly mounted his horse in the envoy's hall; the yamen clerk stopped him; Wu angrily said, "The Minister of Education promised me we would take turns as military governor;
translations.idiomatic: A junior officer named Han Wu repeatedly rode his horse into the commissioner's hall; a clerk tried to stop him. Han Wu snapped, "The Minister Wang promised we would take turns as military governor—

sentences.zh: 上馬何為！」

translations.literal: what harm in mounting a horse!"
translations.idiomatic: what's wrong with riding a horse!"

sentences.zh: 建密遣人刺殺之。

translations.literal: Jian secretly sent men to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian quietly sent assassins to kill him.

sentences.zh: 初，陳敬瑄之拒朝命也，田信孜欲盜其軍政，謂敬瑄曰：「三兄尊重，軍務煩勞，不若盡以相付，日具記事咨呈，兄但高居自逸而已。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Chen Jingxuan defied the court's orders, Tian Lingze wished to seize his military authority and said to Jingxuan, "Third Brother, you are honored and exalted; military affairs are wearisome—better to entrust them all to me; each day I shall compile records and consult and present them; Brother need only sit high and enjoy ease."
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Jingxuan first defied the court's command, Tian Lingze sought to steal control of his army. He told Jingxuan, "Third Brother, you are a man of rank; military business is a burden. Turn it all over to me—I will report daily on affairs, and you need only rest at ease in high station."

sentences.zh: 敬瑄素無智能，忻然許之。

translations.literal: Jingxuan had never possessed wit or talent and gladly agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Jingxuan, who had never been clever, accepted gladly.

sentences.zh: 自是軍事皆不由己，以至於亡。

translations.literal: From then on military affairs were no longer his to decide, until ruin came.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on he controlled nothing in military affairs—and that was how he came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 建表敬瑄子陶為雅州刺史，使隨陶之官，明年，罷歸，寓居新津，以一縣租賦贍之。

translations.literal: Jian memorialized to have Jingxuan's son Tao made prefect of Ya Prefecture, and had Jingxuan accompany Tao to his post; the next year he was dismissed and returned, resided at Xinjin, and was supported from one county's tax revenues.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian petitioned to make Jingxuan's son Tao prefect of Ya Prefecture and sent Jingxuan to accompany him to his post. The next year Jingxuan was relieved and sent home, living at Xinjin and supported by the revenues of one county.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，建分遣士卒就食諸州，更文武堅姓名曰王完阮，謝從本曰王宗本。

translations.literal: On guichou, Jian dispersed soldiers to obtain provisions in the various prefectures, changed Wen Wujian's name to Wang Wanyuan, and Xie Congben's to Wang Zongben.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, Wang Jian sent troops out to live off the various prefectures, renamed Wen Wujian as Wang Wanyuan and Xie Congben as Wang Zongben.

sentences.zh: 陳敬瑄將佐有器干者，建皆禮而用之。

translations.literal: Among Chen Jingxuan's generals and aides, those of ability and capacity Jian all treated with courtesy and employed.
translations.idiomatic: Any capable officer or aide of Chen Jingxuan's, Wang Jian honored and put to use.

sentences.zh: 六軍十二衛觀軍容使、左神策軍中尉楊復恭總宿衛兵，專制朝政，諸假子皆為節度使、刺史，又養宦官子六百人，皆為監軍。

translations.literal: Yang Fugong, Army-Watching Commissioner of the Six Armies and Twelve Guards and chief eunuch of the Left Divine Strategist Army, commanded the palace guard troops, monopolized court governance, and all his adopted sons became military governors and prefects; he also raised six hundred eunuchs' sons, all made army overseers.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong, Army-Watching Commissioner of the Six Armies and Twelve Guards and eunuch-director of the Left Divine Strategist Army, held the palace guards and dominated the court. His adopted sons held posts as military governors and prefects; he raised six hundred eunuchs' sons as well, every one of them an army overseer.

sentences.zh: 假子龍劍節度使守貞、武定節度使守忠不輸貢賦，上表訕薄朝廷。

translations.literal: His adopted sons, Longjian military governor Shouzhen and Wuding military governor Shouzhong, did not submit tribute and taxes, and in memorials ridiculed and slighted the court.
translations.idiomatic: Two of his adopted sons—Shouzhen, military governor of Longjian, and Shouzhong, military governor of Wuding—withheld tribute and submitted memorials mocking the court.

sentences.zh: 上舅瑰求節度使，上訪於復恭，復恭以為不可。

translations.literal: The emperor's maternal uncle Gui sought the post of military governor; the emperor consulted Fugong, and Fugong deemed it impossible.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's uncle by marriage, Gui, sought a military governorship; the emperor asked Yang Fugong, who said it was out of the question.

sentences.zh: 瑰怒，詬之。

translations.literal: Gui was angry and reviled him.
translations.idiomatic: Gui flew into a rage and cursed him.

sentences.zh: 瑰出入禁中，頗用事，復恭惡之，奏以為黔南節度使。

translations.literal: Gui went in and out of the forbidden palace and wielded considerable influence; Fugong hated him and memorialized to appoint him military governor of Qiannan.
translations.idiomatic: Gui had come to wield real power within the palace; Yang Fugong loathed him and had him posted as military governor of Qiannan.

sentences.zh: 至吉柏津，令山南西道節度使楊守亮覆諸江中，宗族賓客皆死，以舟敗聞。

translations.literal: When he reached Jibai Ford, he had the Shannan West-Circuit military governor Yang Shouliang capsize them in the river; kinsmen and guests all died, and it was reported as a shipwreck.
translations.idiomatic: At Jibai Ford he had Yang Shouliang, military governor of Shannan West Circuit, sink Gui's boat in the river. Gui, his kinsmen, and his retinue all perished; the report to court was that the boat had foundered.

sentences.zh: 上知復恭所為，深恨之。

translations.literal: The emperor knew what Fugong had done and deeply resented it.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned what Yang Fugong had done, he hated him bitterly.

sentences.zh: 李順節既寵貴，與復恭爭權，盡以復恭陰事告上，上乃出復恭為鳳翔監軍，復恭慍懟，不肯行，稱疾，求致仕。

translations.literal: Once Li Shunjie had gained favor and rank, he contended with Fugong for power and reported all Fugong's secret doings to the emperor; the emperor then sent Fugong out as army overseer at Fengxiang; Fugong was resentful and indignant, refused to go, claimed illness, and sought retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shunjie, now powerful and favored, wrestled with Yang Fugong for influence and told the emperor everything he knew of Fugong's secret dealings. The emperor thereupon posted Fugong as army overseer at Fengxiang. Fugong, furious, refused to leave, pleaded illness, and asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 九月，乙卯，以復恭為上將軍致仕，賜以幾杖。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on yimao, Fugong was made retired Grand General and granted staff and armrest.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on yimao, Yang Fugong was granted the title of retired Grand General and given the ceremonial staff and seat of retirement.

sentences.zh: 使者致詔命還，復恭潛遣腹心張綰刺殺之。

translations.literal: When the envoy delivered the edict and returned, Fugong secretly sent his trusted follower Zhang Wan to assassinate him.
translations.idiomatic: As the envoy started back after delivering the edict, Fugong secretly sent his confidant Zhang Wan to murder him on the road.

sentences.zh: 加護國節度使王重盈兼中書令。

translations.literal: Wang Chongying, military governor of Huguo, was additionally made Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chongying, military governor of Huguo, was made Chief Secretary as well.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使顧彥朗薨，軍中推其弟彥暉知留後。

translations.literal: Gu Yanlang, military governor of Dongchuan, died; the army acclaimed his younger brother Yanhui as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yanlang, military governor of Dongchuan, died; the troops acclaimed his younger brother Yanhui as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬午，宿州刺史張筠降於丁會。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, on renwu: Zhang Yun, prefect of Su Prefecture, surrendered to Ding Hui.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on renwu, Su Prefecture's governor Zhang Yun surrendered to Ding Hui.

sentences.zh: 癸未，以永平節度使王建為西川節度使；

translations.literal: On guiwei, Wang Jian, military governor of Yongping, was made military governor of Xichuan;
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei, Wang Jian of Yongping was appointed military governor of Xichuan;

sentences.zh: 甲申，廢永平軍。

translations.literal: on jiashen, the Yongping army was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: on jiashen, the Yongping command was abolished.

sentences.zh: 建既得西川，留心政事，容納直言，好施樂士，用人各盡其才，謙恭儉素；

translations.literal: Once Jian had obtained Xichuan, he attended to governance, accepted blunt counsel, took pleasure in generosity and men of talent, employed each man to the full of his ability, and was modest, reverent, and plain in living;
translations.idiomatic: With Xichuan secure, Wang Jian turned his mind to government: he welcomed frank advice, gave freely and delighted in scholars, used every man to the limit of his talent, and lived with modest frugality;

sentences.zh: 然多忌好殺，諸將有功名者，多因事誅之。

translations.literal: yet he was greatly jealous and fond of killing; generals who had won merit and fame were often executed on one pretext or another.
translations.idiomatic: yet he was suspicious and bloodthirsty, and many generals who had won distinction were put to death on one charge or another.

sentences.zh: 楊復恭居第近玉山營，假子守信為玉山軍使，數往省之。

translations.literal: Yang Fugong's residence was near Yushan Camp; his adopted son Shouxin was commander of the Yushan army and often went to visit him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fugong's house stood near Yushan Camp, where his adopted son Shouxin commanded the Yushan garrison and often came to see him.

sentences.zh: 或告復恭與守信謀反，乙酉，上御安喜門，陳兵自衛，命天威都將李順節、神策軍使李守節將兵攻其第。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Fugong and Shouxin were plotting rebellion; on yiyou, the emperor attended at Anxi Gate, arrayed troops for self-defense, and ordered the Tianwei commander Li Shunjie and the Divine Strategist commander Li Shoujie to lead troops in an attack on his residence.
translations.idiomatic: When word came that Fugong and Shouxin were plotting rebellion, the emperor on yiyou went to Anxi Gate, marshaled troops for protection, and ordered Li Shunjie of Tianwei and Li Shoujie of the Divine Strategist Army to assault Fugong's house.

sentences.zh: 張綰帥家眾拒戰，守信引兵助之，順節等不能克。

translations.literal: Zhang Wan led the household retainers in resisting; Shouxin brought troops to help, and Shunjie and the others could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wan rallied the household guard to fight back; Shouxin marched to his aid, and Li Shunjie's force could not break them.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，禁兵守含光門，俟其開，欲出掠兩市，遇劉崇望，立馬諭之曰：「天子親在街東督戰，汝曹皆宿衛之士，當於樓前殺賊立功，勿貪小利，自取惡名。」

translations.literal: On bingxu, the forbidden guard held Hanguang Gate; when it opened they intended to go out and plunder the two markets; they met Liu Chongwang, who reined in his horse and instructed them, saying, "The Son of Heaven is personally east of the street directing the battle; you are all palace guard soldiers—you should kill the rebels before the tower and win merit; do not grasp small gains and earn yourselves an evil name."
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, palace guards holding Hanguang Gate waited for it to open, intending to loot the eastern and western markets. Liu Chongwang intercepted them, reined up, and called out: "The emperor himself is east of the avenue directing the battle. You are palace guards—kill the rebels before the tower and win glory. Do not throw away your honor for petty loot."

sentences.zh: 眾皆曰：「諾。」

translations.literal: All said, "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: "Aye," they answered."

sentences.zh: 遂從崇望而東。

translations.literal: They then followed Chongwang eastward.
translations.idiomatic: They turned and marched east with Liu Chongwang.

sentences.zh: 守信之眾望見兵來，遂潰走。

translations.literal: Shouxin's troops, seeing soldiers coming, fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: At the sight of the approaching force, Shouxin's men broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 守信與復恭挈其族自通化門出，趣興元，永安都頭權安追之，擒張綰，斬之。

translations.literal: Shouxin and Fugong took their clans out through Tonghua Gate and made for Xingyuan; Quan An, chief of Yong'an, pursued them, captured Zhang Wan, and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin and Fugong fled with their families through Tonghua Gate toward Xingyuan. Quan An, chief of the Yong'an guard, pursued them, seized Zhang Wan, and executed him.

sentences.zh: 復恭至興元，楊守亮、楊守忠、楊守貞及綿州刺史楊守厚同舉兵拒朝廷，以討李順節為名。

translations.literal: When Fugong reached Xingyuan, Yang Shouliang, Yang Shouzhong, Yang Shouzhen, and Yang Shouhou, prefect of Mian Prefecture, jointly raised troops to resist the court, in the name of punishing Li Shunjie.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingyuan, Yang Fugong joined Yang Shouliang, Yang Shouzhong, Yang Shouzhen, and Mian Prefecture's Yang Shouhou in raising armies against the court under the banner of punishing Li Shunjie.

sentences.zh: 守厚，亦復恭假子也。

translations.literal: Shouhou was also Fugong's adopted son.
translations.idiomatic: Shouhou, too, was Yang Fugong's adopted son.

sentences.zh: 李克用攻王鎔，大破鎮兵於龍尾崗，斬獲萬計，遂拔臨城，攻元氏、柏鄉；

translations.literal: Li Keyong attacked Wang Rong, inflicted a great defeat on the Zhen army at Longwei Ridge, killed and captured by the ten-thousands, then took Lincheng and attacked Yuanshi and Baixiang;
translations.idiomatic: Li Keyong attacked Wang Rong, crushed the Zhaozhou army at Longwei Ridge with tens of thousands killed or captured, took Lincheng, and pressed Yuanshi and Baixiang;

sentences.zh: 李匡威引幽州兵救之。

translations.literal: Li Kuangwei led You Prefecture troops to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kuangwei marched from Youzhou to his relief.

sentences.zh: 克用大掠而還，軍於邢州。

translations.literal: Keyong plundered extensively and returned, encamping at Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong ravaged the country and withdrew, encamping at Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 十一月，曹州都將郭銖殺刺史郭詞，降於朱全忠。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Guo Zhu, chief commander of Cao Prefecture, killed the prefect Guo Ci and surrendered to Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Cao Prefecture's chief commander Guo Zhu killed Prefect Guo Ci and defected to Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 泰寧節度使朱瑾將萬餘人攻單州。

translations.literal: Zhu Jin, military governor of Taining, led more than ten thousand men to attack Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Jin, military governor of Taining, attacked Shan Prefecture at the head of more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，時溥將劉知俊帥眾二千降於朱全忠。

translations.literal: On yichou, Shi Pu's general Liu Zhijun led two thousand men in surrender to Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Liu Zhijun, a general of Shi Pu, surrendered to Zhu Quanzhong with two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 知俊，沛人，徐之驍將也。

translations.literal: Zhijun was a man of Pei and a fierce general of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhijun was from Pei and one of Xuzhou's fiercest commanders.

sentences.zh: 溥軍自是不振。

translations.literal: From this Shi Pu's army never recovered its vigor.
translations.idiomatic: From that day Shi Pu's army never recovered its strength.

sentences.zh: 全忠以知俊為左右開道指揮使。

translations.literal: Quanzhong made Zhijun Left and Right Vanguard Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong made him commander of the Left and Right Vanguard.

sentences.zh: 辛未，壽州將劉弘鄂惡孫儒殘暴，舉州降朱全忠。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Liu Hong'e, a general of Shou Prefecture, loathing Sun Ru's cruelty and violence, surrendered the entire prefecture to Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Shou Prefecture's Liu Hong'e, disgusted by Sun Ru's brutality, turned the entire prefecture over to Zhu Quanzhong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，乙酉，汴將丁會、張歸霸與朱瑾戰於金鄉，大破之，殺獲殆盡，瑾單騎走免。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on yiyou, the Bian generals Ding Hui and Zhang Guiba fought Zhu Jin at Jinxiang, inflicted a great defeat, killed and captured nearly all, and Jin escaped alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on yiyou, Ding Hui and Zhang Guiba of Bian fought Zhu Jin at Jinxiang, routed his army almost to the last man, and Jin alone escaped on horseback.

sentences.zh: 天威都將李順節恃恩驕橫，出入常以兵自隨。

translations.literal: Li Shunjie of Tianwei, relying on favor, was arrogant and overbearing; going in and out he always had troops attend him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shunjie of Tianwei, swollen with imperial favor, rode everywhere with an armed escort.

sentences.zh: 兩軍中尉劉景宣、西門君遂惡之，白上，恐其作亂。

translations.literal: The two army eunuchs Liu Jingxuan and Ximen Jun then hated him and reported to the emperor, fearing he would stir rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch-directors Liu Jingxuan and Ximen Jun came to loathe him and warned the emperor that he might rebel.

sentences.zh: 戊子，二人以詔召順節，順節入至銀台門，二人邀順節於仗捨坐語，供奉官似先知自後斬其首，從者大噪而出。

translations.literal: On wuzi, the two men summoned Shunjie by edict; Shunjie entered as far as Yintai Gate; the two invited Shunjie to sit and talk in the guard house; the palace attendant Si Xianzhi struck off his head from behind, and his followers raised a great clamor as they burst out.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi the two men summoned him by imperial decree. Li Shunjie entered as far as the Silver Terrace Gate; they invited him to sit and talk in the guardhouse, where the palace attendant Si Xianzhi struck off his head from behind. His escort raised an uproar as they fled.

sentences.zh: 於是天威、捧日、登封三都大掠永寧坊，至暮乃定，百官表賀。

translations.literal: Thereupon the three commands Tianwei, Penglai, and Dengfeng plundered Yongning Ward on a great scale; only at evening did it quiet; the hundred officials submitted congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Tianwei, Penglai, and Dengfeng then looted Yongning Ward until evening. When order returned, the officials offered congratulations.

sentences.zh: 孫儒焚掠蘇、常，引兵逼宣州，錢鏐復遣兵據蘇州。

translations.literal: Sun Ru burned and plundered Su and Chang, led troops to press upon Xuan Prefecture, and Qian Liu again sent troops to seize Su Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru burned and looted Suzhou and Changzhou, marched on Xuanzhou, and Qian Liu once again sent troops to hold Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 儒屢破楊行密之兵，旌旗輜重亙百餘里。

translations.literal: Ru repeatedly defeated Yang Xingmi's troops; banners and baggage wagons stretched more than a hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ru defeated Yang Xingmi again and again; his banners and baggage train stretched for more than a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 行密求救於錢鏐，鏐以兵食助之。

translations.literal: Xingmi sought rescue from Qian Liu; Liu aided him with troops and provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xingmi appealed to Qian Liu for help; Qian Liu sent him troops and supplies.

sentences.zh: 以顧彥暉為東川節度使，遣中使宋道弼賜旌節。

translations.literal: Gu Yanhui was made military governor of Dongchuan, and the palace envoy Song Daobi was sent to bestow regalia.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yanhui was appointed military governor of Dongchuan, and the court envoy Song Daobi was dispatched with the insignia of office.

sentences.zh: 楊守亮使楊守厚囚道弼，奪其旌節，發兵攻梓州。

translations.literal: Yang Shouliang had Yang Shouhou imprison Daobi, seize his regalia, and dispatch troops to attack Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shouliang had Yang Shouhou seize Song Daobi, steal the regalia, and march on Zizhou.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，彥暉求救於王建；

translations.literal: On guimao, Yanhui sought rescue from Wang Jian;
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Yanhui begged Wang Jian for aid;

sentences.zh: 甲辰，建遣其將華洪、李簡、王宗侃、王宗弼救東川。

translations.literal: on jiashen, Jian sent his generals Hua Hong, Li Jian, Wang Zongkan, and Wang Zongbi to rescue Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: on jiashen, Wang Jian sent Hua Hong, Li Jian, Wang Zongkan, and Wang Zongbi to relieve Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 建密謂諸將曰：「爾等破賊，彥暉必犒師，汝曹於行營報宴，因而執之，無煩再舉。」

translations.literal: Jian secretly told the generals, "When you defeat the rebels, Yanhui is sure to reward the army; you, at the camp, answer his feast invitation, and thereby seize him—no need for a second campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian told his generals in secret: "When you break the enemy, Yanhui will certainly feast the army. Accept his invitation at camp and seize him then—no need to fight again."

sentences.zh: 宗侃破守厚七砦，守厚走歸綿州。

translations.literal: Zongkan broke seven of Shouhou's forts; Shouhou fled back to Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zongkan stormed seven of Yang Shouhou's fortresses; Shouhou fled back to Mianzhou.

sentences.zh: 彥暉具犒禮，諸將報宴，宗弼以建謀告之，彥暉乃以疾辭。

translations.literal: Yanhui prepared reward gifts; the generals replied that they would attend the feast; Zongbi told him of Jian's plot, and Yanhui then declined on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yanhui prepared rewards and the generals accepted his invitation to feast—but Wang Zongbi warned him of Wang Jian's plot, and Yanhui pleaded illness and refused.

sentences.zh: 初，李茂貞養子繼臻據金州，均州刺史馮行襲攻下之，詔以行襲為昭信防禦使，治金州。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Maozhen's adopted son Jizhen held Jin Prefecture; Feng Xingxi, prefect of Jun Prefecture, attacked and took it; an edict made Xingxi Defender-in-Chief of Zhaoxin, administering Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Maozhen's adopted son Jizhen had held Jinzhou; Jun Prefecture's Feng Xingxi captured it, and the court appointed Feng defender of Zhaoxin with Jinzhou as his seat.

sentences.zh: 楊守亮欲自金、商襲京師，行襲逆擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Yang Shouliang wished to strike the capital from Jin and Shang; Xingxi met him in counterattack and inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Shouliang tried to strike Chang'an from Jinzhou and Shangzhou, Feng Xingxi counterattacked and routed him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，賜涇原軍號曰彰義，增領渭、武二州。

translations.literal: That year, the Jingyuan army was granted the designation Zhangyi and given additional jurisdiction over Wei and Wu prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Jingyuan army was renamed the Zhangyi command and given Wei and Wuzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 福建觀察使陳巖疾病，遣使以書召泉州刺史王潮，欲授以軍政，未至而巖卒。

translations.literal: Chen Yan, observation commissioner of Fujian, fell ill; he sent an envoy with a letter summoning Wang Chao, prefect of Quan Prefecture, intending to entrust him with military and civil authority; before Chao arrived, Yan died.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan, governor of Fujian, fell ill and sent messengers summoning Quanzhou's Wang Chao to receive command of the province—but Yan died before Wang Chao arrived.

sentences.zh: 巖妻弟都將范暉諷將士推己為留後，發兵拒潮。

translations.literal: Yan's wife's younger brother, chief commander Fan Hui, incited the officers and soldiers to acclaim him as acting governor, and dispatched troops to resist Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's brother-in-law, a chief commander named Fan Hui, persuaded the troops to acclaim him acting governor and marched out to oppose Wang Chao.
